gasflows_sfms_mzr_link.headline: Neutral Gas Flows Linked to Star‑Forming Main Sequence and Metallicity Offsets in 6,000 DESI Galaxies
gasflows_sfms_mzr_link.summary: A study of ~6,000 star‑forming galaxies using Na I D absorption finds that neutral‑gas inflows and outflows produce distinct sSFR and metallicity shifts relative to the SFMS and MZR.
highlights: Outflow hosts (v₍flow₎ ≤ ‑50 km s⁻¹) boost specific star‑formation rates by 0.25‑0.40 dex and raise central metallicities by
Slow inflow hosts (0 < v₍flow₎ < 100 km s⁻¹) increase sSFRs by 0.20‑0.30 dex without notable metallicity changes.
Fast inflow hosts (v₍flow₎ ≥ 100 km s⁻¹) show weaker SFR enhancement and modest metallicity dilution.
Gas‑flow galaxies exhibit systematic offsets in the 4000 Å break strength (Dₙ4000) compared with matched controls.

ru_isotope_late_veneer.institution: Institute(s) of the authors of arXiv:2609.02269v1
ru_isotope_late_veneer.headline: Ruthenium Isotope Split Reveals Mostly Non‑Carbonaceous Late Veneer on Earth
ru_isotope_late_veneer.summary: High‑precision Ru isotope measurements show non‑carbonaceous meteorites follow an s‑process line, while carbonaceous irons form a distinct cluster, suggesting a predominantly NC late‑veneer source for Earth.
highlights: NC meteorites align on an s‑process mixing line in three‑isotope diagrams
CC irons cluster off the NC line, indicating an r‑process excess
Bulk silicate Earth plots on the NC line, implying NC‑dominated late veneer

7.headline: Disorder Can Boost Stability in Power Grids, Brain Networks and Ecosystems
7.summary: Northwestern physicists show that moderate heterogeneity in complex networks often enhances resilience, overturning the long‑held belief that uniformity is optimal.
highlights: A new mathematical framework identifies when node or link variation stabilizes networks
Random differences sometimes outperform perfectly uniform configurations
The effect spans power grids, neuronal circuits, flocking models, architected materials and ecological webs

nanobone_bone_regeneration.headline: Biodegradable Nanobone Boosts Bone Regrowth by Up to 80% in Preclinical Tests
nanobone_bone_regeneration.summary: A calcium‑aluminosilicate nanomaterial developed by University of Sydney researchers accelerates bone formation, activating latent TGF‑β1 and clotting within seconds.
highlights: Nanobone generated ~80% more new bone than control after eight weeks
Activates dormant Transforming Growth Factor β1 at ~10‑fold higher levels
Triggers rapid blood clotting in ~30 seconds, stabilizing injury sites

2609_01796v1.headline: Massive Mergers Trigger Long‑Lived Tumbling of Dark Matter Halos
2609_01796v1.summary: Simulations and TNG50 data show that major galaxy mergers can induce rapid and persistent figure rotation in dark matter halos, preserving a memory of the last merger.
highlights: Transient rotation peaks at 10°‑60° Gyr⁻¹ during satellite infall
Steady tumbling persists at 2°‑40° Gyr⁻¹ for 6‑8 Gyr post‑merger
Radial mergers without orbital angular momentum still drive figure rotation
All six TNG50 halos altered quadrupole orientation during major mergers

turbulent_reconnection_solar_flares.headline: Turbulent Reconnection Accelerates Solar Flare Electrons to ~90 keV
turbulent_reconnection_solar_flares.summary: High‑resolution MHD simulations show that turbulence‑driven compression structures rapidly boost thermal electrons in solar flares to energies near 90 keV, producing observed power‑law spectra.
highlights: Thermal electrons at the flare current sheet and loop top reach ~90 keV
Energy spectra display power‑law indices matching typical flare observations
Acceleration is driven by turbulent compression structures, not termination shocks

ancient_microbe_asgard_imaging.headline: Ancient Stromatolite Microbe Partnership Offers Clues to Origin of Complex Life
ancient_microbe_asgard_imaging.summary: Researchers imaged an Asgard archaeon linked to a bacterium inside modern stromatolites, revealing a possible model for early eukaryotic evolution.
highlights: First direct images of an Asgard archaeon physically connected to a bacterium via nanotubes
Microbe named Nerearchaeum marumarumayae isolated from Shark Bay’s living stromatolites
Electron cryotomography and deep‑learning analysis revealed nutrient‑exchange structures
Study published in Current Biology (2026) after five‑year cultivation effort

new_hall_effect_form.headline: In‑Plane Anomalous Hall Effect Defies Century‑Old Assumption
new_hall_effect_form.summary: Carnegie Mellon physicists have demonstrated an in‑plane anomalous Hall effect, proving the Hall response can arise without a perpendicular magnetic field.
highlights: The team used atomically thin TaIrTe4 coupled with magnetic Cr2Ge2Te6 to generate the new Hall signal.
Both conventional and unconventional Hall voltages were detected in a single ultrathin device.
The discovery could enable planar magnetic sensors that measure multiple field directions simultaneously.

plasmonic_time_crystal.headline: All‑Optical Photonic Time Crystal Demonstrated Using Plasmonic Metamaterial
plasmonic_time_crystal.summary: Researchers in France and Germany have built the first all‑optical photonic time crystal, modulating light at terahertz frequencies within picoseconds.
highlights: The nanostructure uses gold‑capped cavities on an indium‑antimony semiconductor to trap surface plasmons.
THz pulses from the TELBE source at the ELBE accelerator achieved picosecond‑scale optical modulation.
The device halves photon dissipation, opening pathways to THz amplifiers and novel lasers.

bat_dual_antibody_genes.headline: Bats Possess Duplicate Antibody Genes, Explaining Viral Tolerance
bat_dual_antibody_genes.summary: Researchers found that over 500 vesper bat species carry two distinct immunoglobulin heavy‑chain gene sets, a mammalian immune feature never seen before.
highlights: More than 500 vesper bat species have duplicated heavy‑chain antibody loci.
This dual gene system is absent in all other studied mammals.
Study published in Science Advances (2026) by Tulane, Stanford and CDC collaborators.
The discovery suggests a novel mechanism for bats to tolerate many viruses.

immune_switch_aging.headline: Blocking EP2 Receptor in Macrophages Reverses Age‑Related Decline in Mice
immune_switch_aging.summary: Scientists found that disabling the EP2 receptor on tissue‑resident macrophages restores neutrophil clearance, reducing inflammation and keeping multiple organs youthful in aged mice.
highlights: EP2 deletion restored macrophage ability to engulf senescent neutrophils
Older mice lacking EP2 stayed leaner, stronger, and performed memory tests like young mice
Blood‑protein profiles of EP2‑deficient old mice resembled those of youthful controls

electron_spin_surface_reactions.headline: Electron Spin Enables Magnetic Control of Hydrogen Surface Reactions
electron_spin_surface_reactions.summary: Researchers showed that aligning hydrogen electron spin with a magnetic nickel surface can boost adsorption rates by over sevenfold, offering a new reaction control lever.
highlights: Spin‑polarized hydrogen beam was directed at a ferromagnetic nickel surface
Parallel spin orientation increased hydrogen adsorption more than seven times versus perpendicular
Effect vanished on non‑magnetic copper, confirming magnetic origin
Spin alignment also accelerated hydrogen‑deuterium abstraction reactions
External magnetic fields provide a tunable lever for surface chemistry

quantum_material_beating_signal.headline: Korean Team Uncovers Origin of Beating Signal in Topological Insulator Nanowires
quantum_material_beating_signal.summary: Researchers identified that overlapping oscillations from topological surface states and a 2D electron gas cause the puzzling beating observed in Sb‑doped Bi₂Se₃ nanowires.
highlights: Beating arises from superposition of Aharonov‑Bohm oscillations of topological surface states and a 2DEG layer.
Machine‑learning analysis separated the two frequency components, confirming distinct paths with different cross‑sectional areas.
The result provides a definitive criterion for interpreting quantum transport signals in topological insulator devices.

saturn_decagon_discovery_2026_09_03.headline: NASA Finds Giant Decagon Wave Encircling Saturn’s South Pole
saturn_decagon_discovery_2026_09_03.summary: Hubble observations reveal a growing ten‑sided atmospheric wave around Saturn’s south pole, a counterpart to the long‑known northern hexagon, first seen in 2023.
highlights: The decagon was first hinted at in 2023 Hubble images and became clearer by 2025.
It lies within a powerful jet stream and extends through multiple atmospheric layers.
The discovery was enabled by NASA’s OPAL program’s annual Hubble imaging of the outer planets.

ai_suggests_new_physics_experiments.headline: AI designs physics experiments that outperform human‑crafted setups
ai_suggests_new_physics_experiments.summary: A new AI system can automatically combine laboratory components to propose experiments that deliver more precise results than traditional human‑designed designs.
highlights: AI algorithm generated a viable quantum‑optics setup that humans missed
The method improved electron‑microscopy designs, offering clearer images
AI‑driven proposals have already enhanced fusion reactor concepts and gravitational‑wave detector sensitivity

dual_qubit_design.headline: MIT engineers dual‑purpose “arm qubit” to boost speed and slash quantum errors
dual_qubit_design.summary: Researchers at Massachusetts Institute of Technology have simulated a superconducting qubit that separates data storage and interaction, promising faster, higher‑fidelity operations.
highlights: Dual‑purpose design splits data mode and arm mode for dedicated storage and coupling
Quarton coupler provides strong nonlinear coupling while suppressing unwanted mixing
Simulations show state‑of‑the‑art coherence times and accelerated gate speeds

bacterial_nanoplatform_cancer_prevention.headline: Engineered Bacterial Nanoplatform Reprograms Spleen Cells to Halt Cancer Recurrence
bacterial_nanoplatform_cancer_prevention.summary: A bio‑engineered Mycobacterium coated with human serum albumin redirects splenic myelopoiesis, inducing trained immunity that prevents post‑surgical tumor relapse in mice.
highlights: t‑SMC nanoplatform targets spleen via intravenous delivery and releases a TLR7/8 agonist.
Reprogrammed splenic macrophages and stem cells acquire antitumor phenotype and migrate to tumor sites.
In a colon‑cancer recurrence model, 50% of mice showed no tumor return and 62.5% survived long‑term.
Approach converts “cold” tumors into “hot” ones, enhancing response to anti‑PD‑L1 checkpoint blockade.

saturn_decagon_confirmation.headline: Saturn’s South Pole Decagon Confirmed by Hubble Observations
saturn_decagon_confirmation.summary: NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured a fully defined 10‑sided atmospheric wave over Saturn’s south pole, confirming a new planetary phenomenon.
highlights: Decagon first hinted in 2023 Hubble data and sharpened in 2025 images
Amateur and professional astronomers identified the feature in 2024 ground‑based photos
The wave spans multiple atmospheric layers within a powerful jet stream
Study published in Science Advances, September 2026

2609_03051v1.headline: Collective Collapse Can Yield Multiple Primordial Black Holes, Simulations Show
2609_03051v1.summary: New 3+1 numerical-relativity simulations reveal that neighboring curvature perturbations may merge or split, producing single or double primordial black holes.
highlights: Neighbouring curvature peaks can collapse into a single PBH or form a pair of PBHs
A nonspherical quasi‑local compaction diagnostic based on Hawking mass predicts collapse outcomes
The empirical threshold for PBH formation is near \(\mathcal K_{\rm form,c}\approx0.56\)
Maximum curvature alone does not dictate whether one or multiple PBHs form

lvk_o4_catalogue.headline: Fourth LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA Run Yields ~100 New Gravitational‑Wave Detections
lvk_o4_catalogue.summary: The O4 observing run added roughly one hundred fresh mergers, including the loudest signals yet and novel source types, expanding astrophysical insight.
highlights: ~100 new binary‑black‑hole and neutron‑star mergers catalogued
Loudest gravitational‑wave signals recorded to date
Evidence for multiple subpopulations of merging compact binaries

2609_03011v1.headline: Realistic AGN Disk Simulations Reveal How Star Collisions Drive QPEs
2609_03011v1.summary: Two‑dimensional radiation‑hydrodynamic models show that bow‑shock breakout in puffed‑up AGN disks produces X‑ray flares lasting ~10 % of the orbital period, matching QPE observations.
highlights: Simulations use realistic sub‑Eddington AGN disk structure with atmosphere extending to z/r≈1.
Shock breakout at z/r≈0.7 yields flare durations ≈10 % of the star’s orbital period.
More oblique star‑disk impacts generate longer, brighter X‑ray eruptions.
Disk surface density Σ∝r² leads to collisional energy scaling E∝P^{2/3}, reproducing the luminosity‑period trend.

2609_03007v1.headline: Tidal Forces Trigger Chaos in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals Around Supermassive Black Holes
2609_03007v1.summary: A new arXiv preprint shows that external tidal fields break Kerr symmetry, causing chaotic resonances in EMRIs that could affect future gravitational‑wave observations.
highlights: Tidally deformed EMRIs exhibit non‑integrable geodesic dynamics
Poincaré maps reveal two plateaus whose widths grow with tidal field amplitude
Orbit orientation relative to the tidal field strongly influences chaotic behavior

2609_03062v1.headline: DESI DR2 Data Revives Interest in Dynamical Dark Energy Over Dark‑Sector Interactions
2609_03062v1.summary: New DESI DR2, CMB, and supernova measurements favor evolving dark‑energy models while diminishing evidence for a coupling between dark matter and dark energy.
highlights: Interacting $w_0w_a$CDM model with $Q=\beta H\rho_{\rm de}$ shows no significant fit improvement over dynamical dark energy alone.
Thawing and generalized emergent dark‑energy (GEDE) trajectories prefer sizable couplings of opposite signs, unlike the mirage
DESI DR2 combined with Planck and ACT data strengthens the case for a time‑varying dark‑energy equation of state.
Predicted growth signatures differ markedly: enhanced matter clustering for interacting thawing, strong suppression for

2609_03089v1.headline: JWST NIRSpec IFU Maps Reveal Stellar Motions in Three Time‑Delay Lenses
2609_03089v1.summary: Spatially resolved kinematics from JWST‑NIRSpec IFU for HE0435‑1223, PG1115+080 and WFI2033‑4723 tighten mass models, cutting velocity‑dispersion uncertainty to 2.4 %.
highlights: Kinematic maps achieve 6‑11 % total uncertainties per spatial bin
PG1115+080 classified as a fast rotator, the other two as slow rotators
Aperture‑integrated velocity dispersions agree within 0.9σ of previous TDCOSMO values
Data will feed the upcoming TDCOSMO 2026 milestone cosmology analysis

2609_03144v1.headline: Thick CO2‑ or SO2‑Rich Atmosphere Could Survive on Lava World TOI‑561 b
2609_03144v1.summary: New PROTEUS simulations suggest the ultra‑short‑period planet TOI‑561 b may retain a dense CO₂‑ or SO₂‑dominated atmosphere over gigayears despite extreme stellar heating.
highlights: JWST data favor a thick volatile envelope above a global magma ocean
Successful models require a small iron core (≤ 0.40 core radius fraction) and low hydrodynamic escape efficiency (ε ≲ 10⁻³)
Atmospheric pressure today could reach 10³‑10⁴ bar with mean molecular weight of 38‑60 g mol⁻¹

quantum_gravity_experiment.headline: Quantum Galileo Interferometer Confirms Equivalence Principle for 20,000‑Atom Bose‑Einstein Condensate
quantum_gravity_experiment.summary: Physicists at Ben‑Gurion University used a novel interferometer to show that a chilled rubidium cloud obeys Einstein’s equivalence principle in free fall.
highlights: Quantum Galileo Interferometer (QGI) splits a Bose‑Einstein condensate into free‑fall and levitated paths
Interference phase shift matches predictions of the equivalence principle
Experiment employed ~20,000 rubidium atoms cooled near absolute zero

jwst_miri_atmosphere_toi_431b.headline: JWST MIRI Detects Possible Atmosphere on Ultra‑Hot Lava Planet TOI‑431b
jwst_miri_atmosphere_toi_431b.summary: A single JWST MIRI/LRS secondary‑eclipse observation measured an 81 ± 16 ppm depth, suggesting TOI‑431b may retain a thin atmosphere despite its scorching surface.
highlights: Eclipse depth of 81 ± 16 ppm translates to a brightness temperature of 1967⁺²³⁷₋₂⁵³ K
The brightness‑temperature ratio is 0.81 ± 0.10, lower than a bare‑rock model predicts
Comparison with Spitzer data shows a 1.2 σ higher ratio, supporting atmospheric heat redistribution

targeted_search_frbs_magnetars_elliptica.headline: Targeted GBT Survey Finds No Magnetar FRBs in Nearby Elliptical Galaxies
targeted_search_frbs_magnetars_elliptica.summary: A high‑sensitivity L‑band search of five massive ellipticals using GREENBURST and the VEGAS backend detected a background FRB but no magnetar bursts, tightening rate limits.
highlights: FRB 20240817A detected toward M49 (NGC 4472) with 15 ms width and DM = 983 cm⁻³ pc
A cluster of three low‑significance pulses near M49 shows plausible DM = 150‑160 cm⁻³ pc
Joint upper limit on intrinsic burst rate in globular clusters set at R₀ < 0.028 hr⁻¹

bacterial_outer_membrane_proteins.headline: Cryo‑EM snapshots show SurA reshaping to deliver outer‑membrane proteins to the BAM complex
bacterial_outer_membrane_proteins.summary: Researchers used cryo‑electron microscopy to capture four structural states of the SurA‑BAM complex, revealing how SurA’s domains reposition to hand off unfolded proteins for membrane insertion.
highlights: Four distinct cryo‑EM structures of SurA bound to BAM were resolved, showing Core‑only, P1‑visible, P2‑visible, and combined
The flexible P1 domain regulates the Core’s cargo‑binding activity while P2 contacts BamE to bring SurA closer to the assembly
Mutations that disrupt the SurA‑BamE interaction markedly reduce outer‑membrane protein assembly, highlighting a potential

brain_development_2026_09_04.headline: UCLA researchers uncover how metabolism and thalamic signals steer radial glia to shape the human cortex
brain_development_2026_09_04.summary: UCLA scientists show that early brain stem cells integrate glucose‑driven metabolic cues and direct thalamic contacts to decide which cortical neurons to produce.
highlights: Radial glia rely on the pentose phosphate pathway, linking glucose metabolism to cell‑type decisions
Early thalamic projections physically touch radial glia, boosting excitatory upper‑layer neuron formation
NRXN1 mutations alter thalamic signaling, offering a model for autism‑related cortical development

2609_03012v1.headline: Universal CMB Phase Coherence Persists Across All Inflation Energy Scales
2609_03012v1.summary: New analysis shows that the cosmic microwave background’s acoustic peak structure retains identical phase coherence regardless of the inflationary energy scale.
highlights: Phase coherence of primordial perturbations is fixed by the observed primordial spectrum
Curvature perturbation remains conserved on super‑Hubble scales
Result holds for any single‑field inflation scenario and subsequent expansion history

comet_birth_observed.headline: Centaur 450P/LONEOS Shows First Comet‑Like Activity Near Sun
comet_birth_observed.summary: Astronomers observed the centaur 450P/LONEOS developing a bright coma as it approached perihelion, linking inactive centaurs to emerging Jupiter‑family comets.
highlights: Gemini North telescope captured coma formation around 450P between 2019‑2024.
JWST detected carbon‑dioxide gas but no water vapor in the cometary coma.
Close 1992 encounter with Saturn shortened the orbit, bringing perihelion to 5.4 AU.
Crystalline ice signatures suggest thermal processing of primitive outer‑solar‑system material.
Study accepted by Planetary Science Journal and posted on arXiv.

wrinkled_carbon_nitride_photocatalyst.headline: Wrinkled Graphitic Carbon Nitride Upends Flat‑Sheet Photocatalyst Models
wrinkled_carbon_nitride_photocatalyst.summary: New ARC COE‑CSI study shows g‑C₃N₄ layers buckle and shift, overturning the long‑standing flat‑sheet assumption that guided photocatalytic predictions.
highlights: Computational models revealed a lower‑energy buckled structure for g‑C₃N₄ sheets.
X‑ray scattering experiments confirmed the predicted ripples and lateral shifts between layers.
Doping simulations with phosphorus or nickel showed markedly different effects when the wrinkled geometry was used.
The work appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Materials Advances (2026).

dark_matter_signal_2026_09_04.headline: LUX‑ZEPLIN Detector Records Unexplained High‑Energy Event Hinting at Dark Matter
dark_matter_signal_2026_09_04.summary: The LZ experiment observed a single, anomalous particle interaction in 220 live days that resists explanation as known background, sparking cautious excitement.
highlights: A lone event with 2.6‑sigma significance appears in the low‑background region expected for WIMPs
The interaction suggests a possible WIMP mass of at least 200 GeV/c²
The data were collected underground at SURF using 10 tonnes of liquid xenon

seafood_reverse_aging_mice.headline: Sea Squirrel Plasmalogen Supplement Reverses Aging Signs in Mice
seafood_reverse_aging_mice.summary: Dietary plasmalogen from edible sea squirts improved memory, restored brain synapses, reduced inflammation, and regrew darker hair in aged mice.
highlights: Plasmalogen-fed mice reached the Morris water maze platform significantly faster than controls.
Treated mice showed increased synapse numbers and better synaptic integrity.
Brain inflammation was markedly lower in the plasmalogen group.
Aged mice developed thicker, glossier black hair after supplementation.

infant_sun_formation_dust.headline: Ancient Meteorite Dust Reveals Magnetism Shaped Infant Sun’s Birth
infant_sun_formation_dust.summary: Analysis of calcium‑aluminum‑rich inclusions in the 2008 Antarctic meteorite DOM 08006 shows a magnetic field twelve times Earth’s strength during the solar nebula phase.
highlights: CAIs from DOM 08006 retain remanent magnetization indicating a 12‑fold stronger magnetic field than Earth’s.
Magnetic fields likely assisted gravity in flattening the solar nebula into a protoplanetary disk.
The study, published in PNAS on Aug 7, provides the earliest direct evidence of magnetism before the Sun ignited.

mit_bacteria_transistors.headline: MIT Engineers Bacteria as Living Transistors for Plant‑Based Biological Computers
mit_bacteria_transistors.summary: MIT researchers have engineered Pantoea agglomerans cells to act as transistor‑like components, enabling modular living circuits that can perform logic operations and guide chemical signals.
highlights: Two engineered bacterial transistors switch on or off in response to the signaling molecule OC 6
Three relay strains convert output OHC 14 into inputs for downstream transistors
A 24‑colony circuit demonstrated addition of two inputs, taking about eight hours per calculation

mars_deep_heat.headline: Mars Southern Hemisphere Hotter Than Expected Deep Underground, Caltech Finds
mars_deep_heat.summary: Caltech researchers using tidal tomography of spacecraft gravity data discovered a deep thermal anomaly making Mars’ southern interior 200‑400 °C hotter than models predict.
highlights: Thermal anomaly raises temperatures by 200‑400 °C (290‑750 °F) in the southern mantle
Study combines data from Mars Global Surveyor, Mars Odyssey, and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Researchers Alexander Berne and Amirhossein Bagheri published peer‑reviewed results in Nature

dying_radio_galaxies_fade_faster.headline: Young Remnant Radio Galaxies Fade Faster Than Expected, Study Finds
dying_radio_galaxies_fade_faster.summary: Astronomers identified 12 faint remnant radio galaxies aged 8–42 million years, showing that these post‑jet systems disappear much quicker than previously thought.
highlights: Spectral ages range from 8 to 42 million years, with a median of ~12 million years
Higher‑redshift remnants fade more rapidly due to enhanced cosmic‑microwave‑background losses
Multi‑frequency data from MeerKAT, uGMRT, LOFAR, GMRT and the VLA were essential for classification

hidden_order_metasurface_design.headline: Hidden Order in Disordered Metasurfaces Accelerates Nanodevice Design
hidden_order_metasurface_design.summary: Researchers at POSTECH uncovered a repeating Moiré pattern in seemingly aperiodic metasurfaces, enabling rapid analysis of devices containing over a billion nanostructures.
highlights: Discovery of hidden periodicity within complex metasurfaces
Reduction of simulation workload to a few‑dozen nanostructures
Experimental validation of predicted light steering in fabricated devices

ancient_dna_american_cheetah_reassessmen.headline: Ancient DNA Shows Extinct American “Cheetah” Was Arctic‑Adapted Puma Relative
ancient_dna_american_cheetah_reassessmen.summary: Researchers sequenced high‑coverage genomes from Yukon fossils, revealing Miracinonyx trumani was a puma‑like predator that ate fish and thrived far north.
highlights: Miracinonyx trumani’s range extended 20° latitude farther north than previously thought, reaching the Yukon Arctic
Genomic analysis shows it diverged from modern pumas ~2.6 million years ago and evolved convergent cheetah‑like body shape
Stable‑isotope data and loss‑of‑function mutations indicate a diet focused on anadromous fish such as salmon
Both Yukon and Wyoming populations exhibited low genetic diversity but no severe inbreeding bottlenecks

magic_angle_graphene_provides_evidence_f.headline: Screening Electron Interactions Switches Off Superconductivity in Magic‑Angle Graphene
magic_angle_graphene_provides_evidence_f.summary: A new device that screens Coulomb interactions completely suppresses superconductivity and correlated insulating states in magic‑angle twisted bilayer graphene.
highlights: Researchers built a dual‑bilayer device with sub‑nanometer separation to tune screening.
Increasing carrier density in the adjacent layer reduced the critical temperature by over tenfold, eventually eliminating
The results contradict phonon‑mediated models and support electron‑electron interaction driven mechanisms.

sdss_dr20_release.headline: SDSS Releases DR20, Delivering First Southern Hemisphere Optical Spectra
sdss_dr20_release.summary: The twentieth data release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey expands to all‑sky panoptic spectroscopy, adding millions of stellar and galaxy spectra from both hemispheres.
highlights: DR20 provides the first SDSS‑V optical spectra from the Southern Hemisphere
Over 3 million spectra of stars and galaxies are included, plus 18 new value‑added catalogs
The release integrates BOSS data through February 2025 and eROSITA‑matched AGN identifications

archaea_flexitarians_science_advances.headline: Spongic Archaea Reveal Mixotrophic Diet, Consuming Amino Acids
archaea_flexitarians_science_advances.summary: Symbiotic ammonia‑oxidizing archaea in the sponge Ianthella basta were shown to assimilate branched‑chain amino acids, proving they are flexible mixotrophs.
highlights: Nitrosospongia ianthellae cells incorporated labeled valine, leucine and isoleucine in sponge tissue
Genomic transporters for branched‑chain amino acids distinguish sponge symbionts from free‑living relatives
NanoSIMS imaging linked individual archaeal cells to their amino‑acid consumption

the_desi_legacy_imaging_survey_releases_.headline: DESI Legacy Imaging Survey Releases 5.6‑Trillion‑Pixel 2‑D Map of the Universe
the_desi_legacy_imaging_survey_releases_.summary: The eleventh data release (DR 11) unveils a 5.6‑trillion‑pixel map covering 75 % of the sky and cataloguing nearly four billion celestial objects.
highlights: DR 11 combines data from DECam, the Mayall 4‑m telescope, the Bok 2.3‑m, and NASA’s WISE infrared survey.
The map spans roughly 75 % of the celestial sphere in optical and near‑infrared bands.
Nearly four billion objects—including stars, galaxies, quasars, and asteroids—are catalogued for public access via the Legacy
The dataset will guide DESI’s upcoming 3‑D mapping effort and support studies from dark energy to gravitational lenses.

atg2_lipid_transfer_mechanism.headline: Scientists Reveal How Atg2 Binds ER to Drive Autophagosome Formation
atg2_lipid_transfer_mechanism.summary: A team from Science Tokyo discovered that phosphorylation of Atg2’s FF FFAT motif by Atg1 enables binding to VAP proteins, coordinating lipid transfer from the ER during autophagy.
highlights: Atg1 phosphorylates the FFAT region of Atg2, creating a phospho‑FFAT motif that binds the ER‑resident VAP protein Scs2
Both the phospho‑FFAT interaction and the N‑terminal region of Atg2 are required for robust autophagic activity
Human ATG2A/B use MOSPD1/3 homologs via a similar phospho‑FFAT‑like motif, showing conservation from yeast to mammals

asteroid_strength_scaling.headline: Asteroid Bennu’s Surface Is 50 Times Weaker Than Ground Coffee, Study Finds
asteroid_strength_scaling.summary: A new universal scaling framework shows that grain size and shape control asteroid tensile strength, revealing Bennu’s surface strength is under 1 Pa, far weaker than coffee grounds.
highlights: Strength depends on grain size and sphericity, with smaller or more angular particles increasing cohesion
Simulations of granular bridges using LMGC90 reproduced tensile strengths matching Bennu sample measurements
Bennu’s surface strength is estimated below 1 Pa, about 50 × weaker than freshly ground coffee

eight_letter_genetic_alphabet.headline: UC San Diego Shows Enzyme Reads Eight‑Letter DNA Alphabet
highlights: RNA polymerase from E. coli recognized two synthetic base pairs using the same signals as natural ones
High‑resolution cryo‑electron microscopy revealed structural details at sub‑atomic scale
The study appears in Nature Communications (Sept. 2 2026) and is complemented by a related PNAS paper (Aug. 12 2026)
Lead author Dong Wang of UC San Diego highlighted potential for new diagnostics and therapeutics

mercury_core_formation_studies.headline: Mercury’s Graphite Crust and Core Revealed by Lab Simulations
mercury_core_formation_studies.summary: Laboratory experiments reproducing Mercury’s early magma ocean show carbon’s oxidation‑dependent behavior creates a floating graphite crust while keeping the core low in carbon.
highlights: Carbon becomes siderophile under oxidizing conditions, entering the core, but remains in silicate magma under Mercury’s highly
Graphite, being lighter than magma, floats to form a 40–120 m thick primordial crust consistent with MESSENGER observations
The core’s density deficit is explained by silicon and sulfur, not carbon, keeping part of the core liquid for billions of years
Experimental petrology at pressures and temperatures of 1,250–2,170 °C replicates early Mercury conditions

zirconium_pentatelluride_quantum_oscilla.headline: Electrons in ZrTe5 Defy Theory with Reentrant Landau Levels at 60 Tesla
zirconium_pentatelluride_quantum_oscilla.summary: Scientists observed quantum oscillations persisting beyond the quantum limit in zirconium pentatelluride under 0.7 K and 60 tesla fields.
highlights: Quantum oscillations in ZrTe5 remain non‑periodic in 1/B beyond the quantum limit
Spin‑orbit coupling causes Landau levels to back‑bend and re‑enter the Fermi level
Experiments combined 60 tesla pulsed fields at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory

star_formation_stephans_quintet.headline: Turbulent Gas Suppresses Star Formation in Stephan's Quintet
star_formation_stephans_quintet.summary: New ACA CO(1–0) mapping shows that regions with highly turbulent molecular gas in Stephan's Quintet form stars far less efficiently despite abundant gas.
highlights: Molecular gas turbulence correlates with reduced star‑formation efficiency
First detailed ACA CO(1–0) map of the entire Stephan's Quintet group
Interactions disperse gas, preventing gravitational collapse

4.headline: Branched Nanowire LEDs Promise Major Efficiency Gains Over Conventional LEDs
4.summary: Researchers at Lund University have created thin, branched nanowire LEDs that could dramatically increase light output while cutting production costs.
highlights: Light is emitted from side branches thinner than the wavelength, preventing total internal reflection
Only about 4% of light escapes from traditional LEDs without extra surface treatment
The nanowire design separates charge injection from light emission, confirming branch‑originated photons

10.headline: AI Molecule Explorer Maps Millions of Unidentified Small Compounds
10.summary: AIMe uses neuro‑symbolic AI to predict and organize spectra for over 100 million small molecules, expanding searchable chemical space a thousandfold.
highlights: Neuro‑symbolic AI model DeepMS2Reasoner predicts fragmentation pathways for 800 million spectra
MS2KOSMOS database covers essentially all PubChem organic molecules
In mouse gut studies, AIMe identified polyamine derivatives, including a novel macrocyclic polyamine found in 57 of 99 human
At repository scale, AIMe annotated 2.69 million of 7 million spectral clusters in GNPS

levitated_magnet_dark_matter.headline: Levitated Magnet Detector Expands Search for Ultraheavy Dark Matter
levitated_magnet_dark_matter.summary: Rice University scientists used a grain‑sized levitated magnet to probe dark‑matter particles up to ten million times heavier than those examined in prior levitation experiments.
highlights: Floating magnet size comparable to a grain of sand
Sensitivity to motion one‑hundredth of an atom’s width
Search covered nine orders of magnitude in particle mass

embedded_platinum_spin_thermoelectric.headline: Embedded Platinum Channels Enable Bulk Spin‑Based Thermoelectric Conversion
embedded_platinum_spin_thermoelectric.summary: A NIMS‑University of Tokyo composite embeds platinum‑coated YIG powders, allowing spin Seebeck thermoelectric conversion to operate throughout a macroscopic bulk material.
highlights: Platinum‑coated YIG powders were sintered under high pressure to create three‑dimensional nano‑interfaces.
The bulk composite exhibited the spin Seebeck effect, previously limited to thin‑film interfaces.
This “trans‑scale” design enables scaling of thermoelectric output with material thickness.
Results were published in peer‑reviewed Nature Communications (2026).

soft_crosslinking_plastics.headline: Soft‑Crosslinking Strategy Turns Brittle Glassy Plastics Into Tough, Stiff Materials
soft_crosslinking_plastics.summary: Researchers at Tokyo University of Science used bulky DMAP counterions in an ionic comb polymer to achieve unprecedented toughness and stiffness in glassy plastics.
highlights: DMAP acts as both a plasticizer and a physical crosslink, creating a homogeneous nanostructure
The DMAP‑neutralized polymer reaches ~137 MJ/m³ toughness and ~0.9 GPa Young’s modulus
Sodium counterions make similar polymers increasingly brittle, while DMAP maintains performance across concentrations

virus_like_particles_gene_tracking.headline: Engineered Virus‑Like Particles Enable Live‑Cell Transcriptome Tracking Over Time
virus_like_particles_gene_tracking.summary: A new cellular self‑reporting method lets living cells release their RNA in virus‑like particles, allowing repeated, non‑destructive transcriptome analysis of the same cell population.
highlights: Live‑cell transcriptomics achieved without killing cells using engineered virus‑like particles
Method works across immortalized lines, stem‑derived neurons, primary human cells, and organ‑on‑a‑chip models
Researchers captured dynamic gene‑expression changes in endothelial spheroids and vascular‑network formation

earthquake_prediction_method.headline: New GPS Method Pinpoints Sites of Future Megathrust Earthquakes
earthquake_prediction_method.summary: UC Riverside scientists have devised a GPS‑based algorithm that locates locked fault patches where the world’s biggest earthquakes are most likely to rupture.
highlights: The algorithm identified the exact segment of the Kamchatka subduction zone that later produced the 2025 Mw 8.8 quake
It uses interseismic GNSS velocities to map high‑locking probability asperities along major faults
The approach was validated in a peer‑reviewed Geophysical Research Letters (2026) study
Researchers are now extending the method to subduction zones in Japan, Mexico, New Zealand and the Pacific Northwest

lake_networks_carbon_cycle.headline: Lake‑Rich Stream Networks Double Carbon Emissions, Study Finds
lake_networks_carbon_cycle.summary: Researchers in northern Sweden found that networks with tenfold more lake surface area emit nearly twice as much carbon as they transport downstream.
highlights: Ten‑times greater lake surface area lengthened network residence time by ~35‑fold.
Carbon dioxide emissions were 1.8 × higher relative to downstream export.
Measurements covered 32 stream‑lake networks, 42 lakes and over 360 water sections across four seasonal periods.
Summer’s warm, low‑flow conditions amplified emissions, showing a seasonal peak.
Streams still produced more total emissions, but lake‑rich networks shifted a larger share to the atmosphere.

flood_hazard_mapping_2021.institution: University of Potsdam, Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, University of Louvain, Johns Hopkins University
flood_hazard_mapping_2021.headline: 2021 European Floods Exposed Critical Gaps in Hazard Mapping
flood_hazard_mapping_2021.summary: Analysis of 224 deaths in Germany and Belgium shows many victims died outside official flood zones, highlighting urgent need for better risk communication.
highlights: About 50% of deaths in North Rhine‑Westphalia and 75% in Rhineland‑Palatinate occurred outside mapped hazard zones
People over 60 accounted for 72% of fatalities, revealing vulnerability of older adults
Researchers call for revised European Floods Directive to include worst‑case scenarios

human_specific_arhgap11b_marmoset.headline: Human‑Specific Gene ARHGAP11B Drives Neocortex Expansion and Folding in Fetal Marmosets
human_specific_arhgap11b_marmoset.summary: Introducing ARHGAP11B under its human promoter into fetal common marmoset brains increased basal radial glia, upper‑layer neurons, cortical size and induced gyrification.
highlights: ARHGAP11B expression boosted basal radial glia progenitors in the outer subventricular zone
Upper‑layer neuron numbers rose, enlarging the neocortex
The manipulated marmoset cortex developed visible folds, a trait typical of human brains
Study was published as a peer‑reviewed article in Science

bacterial_gasdermins_cell_death.headline: Bacterial gasdermins unveil ancient, phage‑defending cell‑death pathway
bacterial_gasdermins_cell_death.summary: Researchers discovered that diverse bacteria possess gasdermin proteins activated by caspase‑like enzymes, forming pores that block bacteriophage infection.
highlights: Bacterial gasdermins are structural homologs of mammalian pore‑forming cell‑death proteins
Activation occurs via caspase‑like proteases that cleave an inhibitory peptide
The resulting pores protect bacteria from lethal bacteriophage attacks

neurexin_ptpr_synapse_core_module.headline: Neurexin‑T178‑PTPR ternary complexes form a core pre‑synaptic module in mouse brain
neurexin_ptpr_synapse_core_module.summary: A new ternary complex of Neurexins, tetraspanin T178A/B, and LAR‑type PTPRs assembles in the endoplasmic reticulum, organizing synaptic adhesion across the mouse brain.
highlights: Neurexins1‑3, T178A/B, and PTPRD/F co‑assemble via trans‑membrane domains into ~400 kDa complexes
Loss of T178B destabilizes the module, reducing LAR‑PTPR levels and redistributing Neurexins
The ternary complex links pre‑synaptic active‑zone machinery to post‑synaptic receptor networks

type1_diabetes_two_diseases.headline: International GWAS Reveals Two Genetic Subtypes of Type 1 Diabetes
type1_diabetes_two_diseases.summary: A study of 9,091 patients shows HLA‑DR3 and HLA‑DR4 haplotypes drive distinct immune pathways, suggesting type 1 diabetes comprises two genetic forms.
highlights: HLA‑DR3 carriers show mast‑cell–related immune signatures
HLA‑DR4 carriers exhibit T‑cell–driven beta‑cell destruction
The GWAS compared 9,091 type 1 diabetes cases with 14,157 controls
Findings published in Diabetologia suggest personalized treatment strategies

oxr1_bone_loss_mouse_model.headline: OXR1 Emerges as Dual Redox‑Mitochondrial Checkpoint Controlling Osteoclast Differentiation and Bone Loss
oxr1_bone_loss_mouse_model.summary: Researchers show that OXR1 regulates reactive oxygen species and mitophagy in osteoclasts, offering a new therapeutic target for osteoporosis in mice.
highlights: OXR1 expression rises during mouse osteoclastogenesis and is enriched in human osteoclasts
Loss of Oxr1 triggers excess ROS, mitochondrial damage, and impaired autophagic flux
Myeloid‑specific Oxr1 deletion reduces osteoclast formation and increases bone mass
AAV9‑shRNA silencing or pharmacological inhibition of OXR1 mitigates bone loss in an ovariectomy‑induced osteoporosis model

fast_hydrogen_clouds_whirlpool_galaxy.headline: FAST Detects Twin Starless Hydrogen Clouds Near Whirlpool Galaxy
fast_hydrogen_clouds_whirlpool_galaxy.summary: Astronomers using FAST have identified two massive hydrogen clouds around M51 that contain virtually no stars, matching predictions for reionization‑limited dark‑matter halos.
highlights: Each cloud holds ~3 million solar masses of neutral hydrogen but no detectable optical counterpart
Both clouds lie 70–90 kpc from M51 and have total halo masses of ~3.7 billion solar masses
The objects satisfy the RELHIC criteria of compactness, narrow 21‑cm lines (~20 km/s), and lack of stars

ai_fusion_plasma_control.headline: AI System PACMAN Controls Tokamak Plasma in Milliseconds, Predicts Instabilities Ahead
ai_fusion_plasma_control.summary: Princeton researchers demonstrated PACMAN’s AI framework steering DIII‑D plasma in ~20 ms, forecasting a tearing‑mode instability 200 ms before onset.
highlights: PACMAN runs control loops in about 20 milliseconds, far faster than human operators
The AI predicted a tearing‑mode instability 200 milliseconds early and prevented its formation
In five DIII‑D experiments the system coordinated six gyrotrons and adjusted plasma density and rotation

dark_matter_earth_detector.headline: Earth’s Magnetic Cavity Yields Tighter Axion Limits and Mysterious Dark‑Photon Signals
dark_matter_earth_detector.summary: Using the Earth‑ionosphere cavity as a giant detector, researchers set axion interaction limits 100‑times stronger and uncovered unexplained dark‑photon‑like signals.
highlights: New theoretical framework extends reliable predictions up to ~30 Hz
Analysis of a decade of data from the British Geological Survey’s Eskdalemuir Observatory
Axion limits improve by a factor of 100 over previous ground‑based experiments
Several narrow‑band signal candidates consistent with dark‑photon dark matter were found

tree_diversity_climate_extremes_2026.headline: Tree Species Diversity Shields US Forests From Compound Climate Extremes
tree_diversity_climate_extremes_2026.summary: Analysis of 88,116 US forest plots shows that higher tree species diversity improves resistance and recovery during simultaneous heat and moisture extremes.
highlights: Study examined 88,116 forest plots across the United States between 2001 and 2020.
Compound heat‑moisture events reduced forest resistance and recovery more than individual extremes.
Plots with greater tree species diversity suffered smaller productivity declines and rebounded faster.
Findings published in Nature Communications (peer‑reviewed) underscore biodiversity as biological insurance.

operando_electrochemiluminescence_imagin.headline: Operando ECL Microscopy Reveals Particle‑Level Kinetics in Nitrate Reduction
operando_electrochemiluminescence_imagin.summary: A new operando electrochemiluminescence microscopy technique maps nitrate adsorption and nitrite intermediate evolution on single Cu(111) nanosheets, exposing kinetic heterogeneity.
highlights: Operando ECL imaging converts optical signals into spatial descriptors of nitrate adsorption and nitrite formation.
Single‑particle kinetic maps show up to ten‑fold variation among Cu(111) nanosheets.
Interparticle coupling alters intermediate accumulation, affecting apparent catalytic performance under dilute nitrate conditions.
Study appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Nature Communications (2026).

glioblastoma_set_pp2a.headline: Blocking SET Protein Reveals Weak Spot in Deadly Glioblastoma Tumors
glioblastoma_set_pp2a.summary: Researchers at Ohio State University discovered that inhibiting SET restores PP2A activity, preventing tumor formation and sensitizing glioblastoma cells to radiation in preclinical models.
highlights: SET inhibition stopped tumor growth in mouse models
Targeting ANP32A, CIP2A and SET increased radiation sensitivity
Restored PP2A activity undermines glioblastoma’s survival mechanisms
An FDA‑approved antipsychotic boosted PP2A, offering a drug‑repurposing lead

mars_rover_organic_carbon.headline: NASA Perseverance Finds Extensive Macromolecular Carbon in Ancient Martian River Rocks
mars_rover_organic_carbon.summary: Hundreds of macromolecular carbon detections in Jezero’s ancient mudstones suggest complex organics were incorporated during sediment deposition and later groundwater alteration.
highlights: Detection of macromolecular carbon in two Bright Angel formation mudstones
SHERLOC ultraviolet laser fluorescence used to identify organics in sedimentary, carbonate, and sulphate minerals
Perseverance has sealed over two dozen samples for future Mars sample‑return mission

infrared_quantum_emission_boron_nitride_.headline: Tunable Infrared Quantum Emission Predicted from Boron‑Nitride Nanotube Defects
infrared_quantum_emission_boron_nitride_.summary: First‑principles DFT calculations show that intrinsic point defects in single‑walled BNNTs can emit across 1000–3400 nm, tunable by tube diameter, strain, and electric field.
highlights: CB defect ZPL‑like emission spans 1000–2000 nm as tube diameter shrinks from ~0.8 nm to ~0.4 nm
Uniaxial strain shifts emission of the (5,0) BNNT CB defect from 2000 nm up to 2300 nm
Axial electric fields extend the same defect’s emission to 3400 nm
Other defects (CN, CNVB, VB) cover 980–4000 nm ranges under similar tuning

pebbles_and_sand_on_asteroid_162173_ryug.headline: Hayabusa2 Returns Pebbles and Sand from Ryugu’s Subsurface, Confirming In‑Situ Observations
pebbles_and_sand_on_asteroid_162173_ryug.summary: Scientists analyzed >5 g of pebbles and sand returned from asteroid Ryugu, finding morphological matches to the landing sites and confirming the samples’ representativeness.
highlights: Pebbles and sand totaling over 5 g were retrieved in the December 2020 sample return capsule
Morphological analysis shows variations from rugged to smooth, mirroring Ryugu’s surface boulders
The second touchdown captured ejecta from an artificial impact, linking subsurface material to the collected samples

weak_hydrogen_bonds_dethrone_copper_as_t.headline: Weak hydrogen bonds overturn copper’s dominance in metal‑binding stability
weak_hydrogen_bonds_dethrone_copper_as_t.summary: A KAIST team tuned hydrogen‑bonding around transition metals, reversing the Irving‑Williams series and dethroning copper as the most stable binder.
highlights: Hydrogen‑bonding manipulation using flavin‑based ligands reversed the traditional stability order among Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn
Copper’s usual structural distortion is blocked, causing an anti‑Irving‑Williams trend
The study, published in JACS on September 3, shows environmental control can guide selective metal extraction and catalyst design

heliospheric_current_sheet_0_3au.headline: Solar Orbiter Captures Multi‑Layered Heliospheric Current Sheet at 0.3 AU
heliospheric_current_sheet_0_3au.summary: A Solar Orbiter crossing on 13 April 2023 revealed a multi‑layered Heliospheric Current Sheet at 0.3 AU, showing stable ion ratios but variable iron‑to‑oxygen composition.
highlights: Heavy Ion Sensor (SWA‑HIS) detected layered magnetic anomalies and a sudden halt of electron strahls before the main HCS body.
Carbon and oxygen charge‑state ratios remained unchanged across the sheet, confirming freeze‑in heights near 1–2 R☉.
The Fe/O ratio dropped sharply to photospheric levels, likely due to gravity‑driven trapping of iron in closed magnetic loops.
Oxygen temperature spikes exceeded the super‑mass‑proportional limit and correlated with rising O7⁺/O6⁺ ratios, indicating
Protons were observed moving ~50 km s⁻¹ faster, suggesting localized magnetic reconnection sites.

ecological_limit_clearcutting_boreal_bir.headline: Clearcutting Must Stay Below 10% to Preserve Boreal Forest Birds
ecological_limit_clearcutting_boreal_bir.summary: A Finnish study finds that keeping clearcut areas under 10% of the landscape, or a 90‑year rotation, is needed to sustain old‑growth forest bird populations.
highlights: Ecological threshold identified: clearcutting should not exceed ~10% of forest landscape over a decade
Maintaining old‑growth bird populations requires a forest rotation period of at least 90 years
Approximately one‑fifth of boreal forest area must be excluded from clearcut management

antarctic_endemic_microbes.headline: Antarctic Soil Microbes Found to Be Unique to the Continent
antarctic_endemic_microbes.summary: Researchers at University of Colorado Boulder have identified Antarctic Arthrobacter strains that are genetically distinct and exist nowhere else on Earth.
highlights: 90% of the studied Arthrobacter strains are endemic to Antarctica
Genomic analysis compared over 100 Antarctic strains with nearly 500 global samples
Laboratory simulations confirmed these microbes thrive under extreme cold and dryness

single_atom_copper_chains.headline: High‑Pressure Synthesis Yields Record‑Long Single‑Atom Copper Chains
single_atom_copper_chains.summary: Using a diamond anvil cell, researchers transformed blue pigment copper phthalocyanine into ultralong sheathed copper atom chains over 4,000 atoms long.
highlights: Copper phthalocyanine crystals were compressed to >21 GPa, converting them into micrometer‑scale atomic wires
The resulting sSMACs feature a triple‑layer carbon‑nitrogen sheath that stabilizes the copper core
Electrical conductivity is ten times higher along the wire than across it, driven by the surrounding carbon framework
The chains remained intact after exposure to acidic solutions and ultrasonic vibration

american_cheetah_reclassification.headline: American “cheetah” turned out to be a distant puma relative, not a true cheetah
american_cheetah_reclassification.summary: New DNA and isotope analysis shows the extinct Miracinonyx trumani was more closely related to modern pumas and adapted to diverse diets, including fish in the Arctic.
highlights: Miracinonyx trumani DNA links it to pumas, diverging 2.6 million years ago
Yukon specimens reveal a fish‑based diet, unlike Wyoming individuals that ate terrestrial herbivores
Study expands the species’ known range 1,400 miles northward, into Beringia

white_dwarf_binary_gw_candidate.headline: Ultracompact White‑Dwarf Pair eRASSU J0608 Shows Rapid Orbital Decay
white_dwarf_binary_gw_candidate.summary: Astronomers using NICER and Einstein Probe have identified the binary white dwarf eRASSU J0608, whose six‑minute orbit is shrinking fast enough to emit detectable gravitational waves.
highlights: The system pulses every 374 seconds, indicating a six‑minute orbital period.
Orbital decay matches predictions from gravitational‑wave energy loss, one of the fastest observed for a binary star.
Estimated chirp mass is 0.43 solar masses, making it a strong gravitational‑wave source.
Future space‑based detectors like LISA could directly observe its waves if the distance is favorable.

80000_year_old_arrowheads_rewrite_human_.headline: 80,000‑Year‑Old Arrowheads from Uzbekistan Challenge Timeline of Homo sapiens Arrival in Europe
80000_year_old_arrowheads_rewrite_human_.summary: Tiny triangular projectile points dated to 80 ka at the Obi‑Rakhmat site in Uzbekistan resemble later French arrowheads, suggesting early sophisticated weaponry in Central Asia.
highlights: Obi‑Rakhmat rock shelter yielded unretouched microlithic points less than 2 cm wide
Points match micro‑arrowheads from Mandrin, Rhône Valley, France dated to ~54 ka
Study published in PLOS One (2025) argues for independent Central Asian invention of arrow technology
Genetic work by Vallini and Mazières identifies the Persian Plateau as a hub for early non‑African populations

psychological_stress_increases_skin_infe.headline: Stress‑Induced TGFβ Suppresses Antimicrobial Fibroblasts, Heightening Staphylococcus aureus Skin Infection
psychological_stress_increases_skin_infe.summary: Psychological stress triggers adrenergic signaling that raises TGFβ, dampening fibroblast‑derived cathelicidin and increasing susceptibility to Staphylococcus aureus skin infection in mice.
highlights: Adrenergic activation during stress induces TGFβ production in dermal fibroblasts
Elevated TGFβ suppresses cathelicidin (Camp) antimicrobial peptide expression
Blocking adrenergic or TGFβ signaling restores fibroblast antimicrobial function and infection resistance

catalysis_advanced_oxidation.headline: High‑Loading Cobalt Pyroborate on Fibrous Silica Boosts Wastewater Oxidation
catalysis_advanced_oxidation.summary: A Co₂B₂O₅@KCC‑1 catalyst achieves up to 4.6‑fold faster degradation of 4‑NP, tetracycline and sulfamethoxazole via sulfate‑radical advanced oxidation, while remaining recyclable.
highlights: Optimized Si/Co = 6, B/Co = 1.5 composition delivers 1.6‑ to 4.6‑fold activity gains over comparable Co‑based catalysts.
Uniform Co₂B₂O₅ dispersion on radially porous KCC‑1 enhances active‑site accessibility and mass transport.
ROS tests confirm generation of surface‑bound SO₄•⁻ radicals and singlet oxygen (¹O₂) during PMS activation.
Catalyst retains structure and performance after multiple cycles in natural river water containing organic matter.

ingestible_bacterial_electronic_system.headline: Ingestible Bacterial‑Electronic Device Detects Gastrointestinal Bleeding in Real Time
ingestible_bacterial_electronic_system.summary: Researchers engineered a probiotic sensor and ultra‑low‑power capsule that wirelessly reports blood presence in the gut of pigs and mice.
highlights: Engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 senses heme via HrtR and ChuA, producing luminescence detectable by the capsule
The IMBED capsule uses a 5 mAh battery to power a nanowatt luminometer, transmitting data wirelessly for up to 1.5 months
In vivo tests showed an 18‑fold luminescence increase after indomethacin‑induced bleeding in C57BL/6J mice
Device sensitivity reaches 5 × 10⁴ photons s⁻¹, detecting blood as low as 32.5 ppm in vitro

cmb_structures_deep_learning_2026.headline: Deep Learning Maps Six Continuous Heterogeneity Belts at Earth's Core‑Mantle Boundary
cmb_structures_deep_learning_2026.summary: A deep‑learning analysis of over 2 million seismic records uncovered six continuous scattering belts at the core‑mantle boundary, vastly expanding prior data.
highlights: Identified 174,929 PKP precursor signals, about ten times previous global totals.
Six continuous heterogeneity regions span the North Atlantic, northern Eurasia, South Atlantic, Southern Africa, Pacific and
Maps align with known ultra‑low‑velocity zones, suggesting ancient subducted slabs and localized melting.

2609_05053v1.headline: Unite Supernova Sample Tightens Dark Energy Constraints with 2884 Type Ia Explosions
2609_05053v1.summary: Combining Pantheon+ and DES‑SN5YR, the new Unite dataset of 2884 Type Ia supernovae yields Ω_m = 0.310 and hints of evolving dark energy.
highlights: Unite merges Pantheon+ and DES‑SN5YR into the most internally consistent SN Ia sample to date
Flat‑ΛCDM fit gives Ω_m = 0.310^{+0.012}_{-0.011} using supernovae alone
Joint analysis with CMB, DES and DESI BAO shows tension that eases when allowing w(z) to vary

2609_05312v1.headline: JWST Detects Transit Timing Variations Hinting at Hidden Planet Around LP 890‑9
2609_05312v1.summary: Analysis of 20 JWST/NIRSpec PRISM transits of LP 890‑9b and c reveals timing shifts that suggest a third planet, LP 890‑9d, with an orbital period near 4.4 days.
highlights: Peak‑to‑peak TTV amplitudes reach ~17 s for b and ~35 s for c
Two‑planet models cannot reproduce the observed TTV super‑period
Three‑planet fits place a candidate LP 890‑9d between b and c

2609_04308v1.headline: Supernova Microlensing Offers New Window onto Ultracompact Minihalos and Primordial Power
2609_04308v1.summary: A proposed method uses LSST supernova microlensing to detect ultracompact minihalos, linking their abundance to constraints on the early‑Universe power spectrum.
highlights: Supernova microlensing can reveal lenses up to ~pc scales for masses around 10^4 M⊙
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s LSST will provide a massive supernova sample for this search
Projected limits on minihalo abundance translate into bounds on small‑scale primordial power

inflows_galaxies_2026.headline: DESI Survey Finds Inflows in Up to Half of Galaxies, Revealing Baryonic Cycling
inflows_galaxies_2026.summary: A new analysis of ~30,000 galaxies using DESI spectroscopy shows coherent inflowing gas at ~100 km/s in 20‑50% of the sample, overturning expectations about gas flows in star‑forming versus quiescent systems.
highlights: Inflows detected in 20‑50% of galaxies, including many quiescent types
Star‑forming galaxies mainly exhibit bound outflows, suggesting a galactic fountain recycling on ~0.5 Gyr
Detected inflows are metal‑rich, implying recycled halo gas rather than pristine accretion

2609_04597v1.headline: NASA's Habitable World Observatory Could Detect Ocean Glint on Earth‑Like Exoplanets
2609_04597v1.summary: Simulated observations show that a phase angle of at least 120° and signal‑to‑noise ratios between 5 and 25 enable reliable detection of ocean glint signatures.
highlights: Glint detection requires phase angles ≥120°
Signal‑to‑noise ratios of 5–25 are sufficient for retrievals
Model selection confirms glint presence over non‑glint models

rapid_quenching_protocluster_z2_2.headline: Gas‑depleted, quenched galaxies discovered in the Spiderweb protocluster at z = 2.16
rapid_quenching_protocluster_z2_2.summary: A stacked analysis of HST, JWST and ALMA data reveals massive galaxies in the Spiderweb core that stopped forming stars about 500 Myr ago and retain less than 7 % of their gas.
highlights: Stacked HST F160W, JWST Paβ imaging and ALMA 1.2 mm data constrain star‑formation histories and gas content
Average gas fraction fgas < 7 % for the quiescent population
Rapid quenching occurred ≈500 Myr before observation, matching progenitor HAEs

2609_04313v1.headline: Environmental Multitracer Method Boosts Primordial Non‑Gaussianity Constraints for DESI LRGs
2609_04313v1.summary: A new technique that splits galaxy samples by large‑scale dark‑matter environment halves the uncertainty on local‑type primordial non‑Gaussianity, reaching σ(f NL)≈1.
highlights: Multitracer analysis uses dark‑matter environment instead of halo mass or secondary properties
Validated with N‑body and Quijote simulations showing unbiased f NL recovery
DESI LRG forecasts predict a 2‑3× improvement over single‑tracer methods

2609_04991v1.headline: New Method Refines Dark Siren Cosmology and Updates Hubble Constant Measurement
2609_04991v1.summary: Researchers introduce a sampled redshift prior to jointly infer galaxy host properties and cosmology, yielding H₀ = 71.9⁺⁹·¹₋⁷·⁵ km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
highlights: Joint inference of host‑galaxy weighting model achieved for the first time
Updated Hubble constant value aligns with previous GWTC‑5.0 results
Method mitigates galaxy catalogue incompleteness and redshift uncertainties

2609_04312v1.headline: ALPACA Pipeline Cuts JWST Lens Modeling Time to Hours, Controls PSF Systematics
2609_04312v1.summary: A new GPU‑accelerated pipeline, ALPACA, jointly reconstructs source galaxies and PSF for JWST lensing, reducing runtimes to under 15 hours while keeping H₀ bias below one percent.
highlights: ALPACA reduces per‑system modeling time from weeks to <15 hours using GPU acceleration
Joint source‑pixel and PSF reconstruction limits DΔt bias to the percent level
Validated on realistic JWST/NIRCam mock data built from COSMOS galaxies

2609_05128v1.headline: Isolated Binary Evolution Could Yield Unequal‑Mass Black‑Hole Mergers With High‑Spin Primaries
2609_05128v1.summary: Researchers propose two isolated‑binary pathways that may produce unequal‑mass binary black‑hole mergers featuring a primary black hole spinning near 0.7, challenging the need for hierarchical mergers.
highlights: Mass‑ratio reversal in wide binaries can spin up and enlarge the second‑born black hole
Chemically homogeneous evolution of a close primary star can create a massive, high‑spin first‑born black hole
Large natal kicks or tertiary‑induced Kozai‑Lidov oscillations can generate significant spin‑orbit misalignments

2609_04334v1.headline: BAO Data Point at z = 0.706 Drives Dark‑Energy Tension in Predictive Tests
2609_04334v1.summary: A leave‑one‑redshift‑block cross‑validation shows that a single DESI DR2 BAO measurement, not supernovae, favors evolving dark energy over ΛCDM.
highlights: ΔELPD scoring finds modest preference for w₀wₐCDM driven by BAO
The LRG2 block at z = 0.706 supplies the entire BAO preference
All SNIa datasets show ΔELPD consistent with zero, indicating no predictive tension

2609_05230v1.headline: ALMA Detects Gas Gaps and Kinematic Signatures Linked to Giant Protoplanets in WISPIT 2 Disk
2609_05230v1.summary: High‑resolution ALMA observations reveal co‑located gas gaps and rotation anomalies in the WISPIT 2 protoplanetary disk, matching the positions of previously imaged giant protoplanets.
highlights: Gas gaps appear in the 12CO integrated intensity map and its rotation curve
The gaps exhibit eccentric shapes consistent with massive planet‑disk interaction models
An outer disk lacking eccentricity suggests a third unseen planet may be present

immune_aging_mice.headline: Blocking EP2 Receptor Reverses Aging Signs in Mice
immune_aging_mice.summary: A Stanford study published in Science shows that disabling the EP2 receptor in tissue‑resident macrophages restores youthful inflammation patterns and improves memory, frailty, muscle and heart function in older mice.
highlights: EP2 signaling was blocked using drugs and genetic editing in aged mice
Restored clearance of senescent neutrophils by tissue‑resident macrophages
Observed improvements in memory, frailty, muscle mass and cardiac performance

quantum_phases_chromium_spin_triplet.headline: Three distinct spin‑triplet phases discovered in potassium chromium arsenide
quantum_phases_chromium_spin_triplet.summary: Researchers at Okayama University identified three spin‑triplet superconducting phases in K₂Cr₃As₃, revealing topological properties and potential for fault‑tolerant quantum computing.
highlights: Three superconducting phases (A, B, C) appear under different magnetic‑field strengths applied along the crystal c‑axis
Phase B breaks time‑reversal symmetry while Phase C hosts a line node in the superconducting gap
The material’s transition temperature is 6.2 K, the highest reported for a spin‑triplet superconductor
Nuclear magnetic resonance was essential for probing spin susceptibility in the superconducting state

shmr_dwarf_desi_dr1.headline: DESI Data Release 1 Extends Stellar‑to‑Halo Mass Relation into Dwarf Galaxy Regime
shmr_dwarf_desi_dr1.summary: Using DESI DR1, researchers map the stellar‑to‑halo mass relation down to galaxies with stellar masses below 10⁹ M⊙, revealing steeper slopes and larger scatter at dwarf scales.
highlights: DESI Bright Galaxy Survey provides clustering, lensing, and satellite occupation measurements for 12 stellar‑mass samples
Average halo‑to‑stellar mass relation follows log⟨M_h⟩=12.06+0.58 log(M_★/10¹¹)+(M_★/10¹¹)^0.73
Power‑law slope of the SHMR steepens from 0.32 ± 0.06 at Milky Way masses to 2.08 ± 0.21 in dwarf galaxies
Scatter in the SHMR grows from 0.17 dex to 0.68 dex when moving from Milky Way‑like to Large Magellanic Cloud‑like systems

noise_entanglement.headline: Noise‑Engineered Entanglement Links Distant Qubits Without Active Pulses
noise_entanglement.summary: Researchers at ISTA demonstrated that correlated microwave noise can autonomously entangle two transmon qubits over a metre, offering a continuous‑time quantum link.
highlights: Entanglement achieved using a Josephson parametric converter that splits pump photons into correlated gigahertz pairs.
Two transmon qubits separated by a metre of coaxial cable settle into a dark entangled state while the field remains on.
The protocol requires no synchronized pulses, heralding, or feedback, reducing overhead for scalable quantum networks.
Measured concurrence is 0.10, representing about ten percent of the original continuous‑variable entanglement.

gaia_quiet_bh_discoveries.headline: Quiet Black Holes with Stellar Companions Challenge Formation Theories
gaia_quiet_bh_discoveries.summary: Three silent stellar‑mass black holes identified by Gaia’s precise astrometry reveal unexpected close companions, prompting new questions about their binary formation pathways.
highlights: Gaia detected three inactive black holes by observing stellar wobbles without seeing a luminous companion
Two systems (BH1 and BH2) have unusually close orbits despite the progenitor star’s expansion
Roche Lobe Overflow may allow mass transfer without merging, preserving the binary
The study is based on a peer‑reviewed paper in the Astrophysical Journal (2026)

dwarf_agn_jwst_nirspec.headline: JWST NIRSpec Uncovers Varied Nuclear Environments in Dwarf AGN Hosts
dwarf_agn_jwst_nirspec.summary: Using JWST/NIRSpec IFU, astronomers mapped the central kiloparsec of four dwarf galaxies, finding over 100 emission lines and diverse gas and dust signatures.
highlights: Over 100 emission lines detected, including coronal lines with ionization potentials >300 eV
Hot dust contributes strongly to the infrared continuum in two of the galaxies
PAH and coronal line emission observed within 100 pc of the nuclei in three galaxies
Hot H₂ gas mass estimated at 1–20 M⊙ within 300 pc, showing both thermal and non‑thermal excitation

shared_genetic_roots_ocd_tourette_autism.headline: Rutgers Team Identifies 36 Shared Risk Genes Linking OCD, Tourette and Autism
shared_genetic_roots_ocd_tourette_autism.summary: A new Nature Neuroscience study expands known high‑confidence genes to 36, revealing strong genetic overlap among OCD, chronic tic disorders and autism.
highlights: 36 genes now linked to OCD and chronic tic disorders, many also associated with autism and schizophrenia
Risk variants can increase disease odds up to 210‑fold, with an average 57‑fold effect
Analysis of nearly 4,000 cases—including 2,400 parent‑child trios—highlights the cortico‑striato‑thalamo‑cortical circuit

reversible_electric_control_chiral_phono.headline: Electric Field Switches Handedness of Chiral Phonons in BaTiO₃ Device
reversible_electric_control_chiral_phono.summary: Researchers demonstrated that a reversible 3 V electric field can flip and retain the chirality of phonons in a 40 nm BaTiO₃ membrane at room temperature.
highlights: Chiral phonon handedness reverses when the ferroelectric polarization of BaTiO₃ is switched
The switched state persists after the electric field is removed
Circularly polarized X‑rays at ESRF were used to read phonon chirality via RIXS

desi_dr11.headline: DESI Legacy Imaging Survey Unveils 5.6‑Trillion‑Pixel 2D Cosmic Map
desi_dr11.summary: The DESI Legacy Imaging Survey’s 11th data release presents a 5.6‑trillion‑pixel map of nearly 4 billion objects, covering 75 % of the sky.
highlights: The map contains ~4 billion stars, galaxies, quasars and asteroids across 75 % of the sky.
Data were captured with DECam on the 4‑meter Mayall telescope, the 2.3‑meter Bok telescope, and NASA’s WISE.
The release supports DESI’s goal to build the largest high‑resolution 3D map for dark‑energy studies.
More than 160 scientists contributed, linking the survey to upcoming Rubin and Roman observatories.

deep_biosphere_persistence.headline: Deep Biosphere Survived Caledonian Mountain Building and Erosion for 378 Million Years
deep_biosphere_persistence.summary: Microbial methanogenesis persisted in a 2.3‑km deep Swedish borehole, with episodic activity spanning from 378 million to 1.8 million years ago.
highlights: Mineral‑scale carbon isotope signatures reveal ancient methane‑producing microbes
U–Pb dating links microbial bursts to major tectonic uplift and erosion events
Study based on fracture‑filling calcite from the COSC‑2 drill core in central Sweden

selfprocessingbrain_jneurosci_2026.institution: Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
selfprocessingbrain_jneurosci_2026.headline: Self‑Processing Brain Networks Show Conservation and Reorganization Across Primates
selfprocessingbrain_jneurosci_2026.summary: Researchers compared structural and gene‑expression data in humans, chimpanzees and macaques, finding conserved interoceptive circuits but divergent abstract self‑processing pathways.
highlights: Small‑scale brain structure and gene expression are highly similar between humans and macaques
Large‑scale connectivity reveals chimpanzees as an intermediate between macaques and humans
Interoceptive processing aligns macaques with chimpanzees, while exteroceptive processing aligns chimpanzees with humans
Abstract mental self‑processing shows the greatest species differentiation

climate_amplifies_earthquakes_arctic.headline: Climate Change Amplifies Earthquake‑Triggered Avalanches on Jan Mayen’s Permafrost‑Bound Slopes
climate_amplifies_earthquakes_arctic.summary: A 6.5‑magnitude quake on Jan Mayen in March 2025 caused a rock avalanche, with warming‑induced permafrost loss making the volcanic slope unusually vulnerable.
highlights: The March 10 2025 quake (M 6.5) triggered a massive rock avalanche on the Kjerulf Glacier
Permafrost thaw reduced ice cement that stabilised the volcanic slope of Beerenberg
Satellite data showed unprecedented debris spread and calving at neighboring Weyprecht Glacier
Study published in PNAS demonstrates climate‑driven amplification of seismic hazards in the Arctic

scientists_observe_einstein_s_gravity_in.headline: Einstein’s Equivalence Principle Holds for Falling Quantum Atoms in First Direct Test
scientists_observe_einstein_s_gravity_in.summary: Physicists used ultracold rubidium atoms in a Quantum Galileo Interferometer to directly observe the predicted quantum phase shift under gravity, confirming Einstein’s principle at the quantum level.
highlights: Quantum phase shift measured matches Einstein’s equivalence principle prediction
Experiment split rubidium atom wave into stationary and free‑falling paths using magnetic fields
Team included Nobel‑winning Sir Roger Penrose and researchers from Ben‑Gurion University, Oxford and Ulm

hubble_webb_tno.headline: Hubble and Webb Reveal Tiny TNOs Preserve Early Solar System Secrets
hubble_webb_tno.summary: Joint Hubble‑Webb observations of 27 ultra‑faint Trans‑Neptunian Objects show they retain the same colors and size distribution as larger siblings, challenging collision models.
highlights: 27 new TNOs detected, including one as faint as fireflies on the Moon
Smallest observed TNO measures ~5 km (3 mi) in diameter
Both hot and cold TNO populations share identical color‑size relationships

early_statin_dementia_risk.headline: Early Statin Use Cuts Dementia Risk by 15% in Diabetics
early_statin_dementia_risk.summary: A Danish cohort of 132,585 newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients showed a 15 % lower dementia risk over ten years when statins were started within one year.
highlights: Statin initiation within one year of diagnosis reduced dementia risk by 15 % relative to no early treatment
Starting statins between one and five years after diagnosis still lowered risk, but by only 10 %
Only 2.7 % of participants developed dementia during a median 7.1‑year follow‑up

glueball_candidate_decay.headline: BESIII Finds Strongest Evidence Yet for Long‑Sought Glueball X(2370)
glueball_candidate_decay.summary: Using 10 billion J/ψ decays, BESIII researchers identified X(2370) as a glueball‑dominated particle, noting a missing kaon‑pair decay that supports its gluon‑only nature.
highlights: X(2370) spin‑parity matches predictions for the lightest glueball.
The kaon‑pair decay channel is limited to ≤8 % of the dominant decay mode.
Analysis used the full 10 billion J/ψ dataset from the BEPCII collider.
Results are presented in a preprint on arXiv and at the International Conference on High Energy Physics.

personality_gwas_big5.headline: Over 1,200 Genetic Variants Linked to Big Five Personality Traits
personality_gwas_big5.summary: An international consortium identified more than 1,200 DNA variants associated with the Big Five traits, revealing extensive genetic ties to health, income and lifestyle outcomes.
highlights: 1,200+ variants correlate with openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism
Combined genetic effects are sizable despite tiny individual impacts
Same variants predict personality across ages and continents

gut_asthma_connection.headline: Gut‑Linked Immune Shifts Found in Fatal Asthma Cases
gut_asthma_connection.summary: A study of 695 organ donors reveals that fatal asthma attacks involve heightened type‑2 inflammation and altered immune cells in gut‑associated lymph nodes.
highlights: All 41 fatal‑asthma donors had IgE levels above the reference threshold
Lung tissue showed increased type‑2 helper T cells, innate lymphoid cells, and mast cells
Gut‑associated lymph nodes displayed stronger immune connections than in non‑asthma donors

moon_formation_impact_2026.headline: Temperature-Dependent Material Strength Alters Moon Formation in New Impact Simulations
moon_formation_impact_2026.summary: New SPH simulations show that hotter, weaker Theia leads to an intact Moon, while cooler, stronger Theia produces a debris disk, reshaping giant impact models.
highlights: Hot, weak Theia yields an intact Moon within five hours of impact
Cool, strong Theia generates a classic protolunar debris disk
Inclusion of temperature‑dependent material strength changes momentum transfer and accretion percentages
Simulations align with prior models for hot collisions but diverge for cool scenarios

rattlesnake_antivenom_discovery.headline: Rattlesnake Blood Yields Antivenom Ten Times More Potent Than Current Treatment
rattlesnake_antivenom_discovery.summary: Researchers combined rattlesnake serum proteins to create an antivenom that proved about ten times more effective than existing commercial snakebite therapy in lab tests.
highlights: Combination of FETUA proteins blocked lethal effects of multiple viper venoms
Optimized protein mixtures were ~10‑fold more potent than sheep‑derived antivenom
Study published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2026

copd_late_stage_trial.headline: AstraZeneca’s tozorakimab cuts COPD flare‑ups by 30% in Phase 3 trials
copd_late_stage_trial.summary: Late‑stage Phase 3 studies show AstraZeneca’s injectable drug tozorakimab reduces COPD exacerbations by roughly 30% over a year, offering a new therapeutic option.
highlights: tozo lowered COPD exacerbations by about 30% across all patients
Phase 3 trials included participants ineligible for existing COPD drugs
Results presented at the European Respiratory Society conference in Barcelona and published in the New England Journal of Medicine

fast_growing_blackholes_2026.headline: eROSITA Finds Eight Supermassive Black Holes Growing Ten Times Faster Than Their Galaxies
fast_growing_blackholes_2026.summary: A new eROSITA survey of over 20,000 quasars reveals eight black holes that comprise about 5 % of their host galaxies’ mass and may double in size within a billion years.
highlights: Eight quasars show a black‑hole‑to‑galaxy mass ratio of ~20 : 1 instead of the typical ~200 : 1
These over‑massive black holes account for roughly 5 % of their galaxies’ total mass
Three of the eight are among the brightest quasars, indicating extreme accretion rates
The study used eROSITA X‑ray data combined with optical/infrared galaxy brightness measurements

siberian_methane_regimes_2026.headline: Arctic warming splits Siberia into wet and dry methane‑emitting regimes
siberian_methane_regimes_2026.summary: Rising Arctic temperatures are creating contrasting climate regimes in western and eastern Siberia, driving a 5% annual rise in methane emissions from the region.
highlights: Western Siberia’s wetlands are getting wetter, boosting microbial methane release from thawing permafrost
Eastern Siberia is drying, increasing wildfire‑driven methane emissions
Methane emissions grew by about 13.2 million tons between 2010‑2023, a 5% yearly increase
Satellite‑based methane flux inversion limited estimate uncertainty to roughly 10%

sparse_data_sst_method.headline: Sparse-data method boosts global sea surface temperature estimates by 40%
sparse_data_sst_method.summary: A new Sparse Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method (S-DEIM) predicts sea surface temperatures 40% more accurately than traditional DEIM and outperforms top AI models.
highlights: S-DEIM achieved 40% higher accuracy than the classic DEIM approach
S-DEIM was 2% more accurate than the best‑performing convolutional neural network
Training time dropped from 1½ hours to one minute
The test used 30 years of NOAA SST observations, withholding the final year for validation

rewired_ribosomes.headline: Engineered Ribo‑M Ribosomes Dedicated to Single‑Protein Production
rewired_ribosomes.summary: University of Illinois Chicago scientists have created Ribo‑M, a ribosome permanently linked to its mRNA, enabling focused synthesis of one protein.
highlights: Ribo‑M physically links a ribosome to its messenger RNA, eliminating the search for genetic instructions
The platform successfully produced fluorescent, antibiotic‑resistance, and light‑emitting proteins in bacterial tests
Future designs aim to incorporate non‑canonical amino acids for more stable therapeutic proteins

antibiotic_efflux_mechanism.headline: University of Osaka uncovers new fosfomycin efflux pump in Streptococcus pneumoniae
antibiotic_efflux_mechanism.summary: Researchers identified the ABC transporter FoeAB that actively exports fosfomycin, revealing a novel resistance mechanism in the pneumonia‑causing Streptococcus pneumoniae.
highlights: The previously unknown ABC transporter FoeAB increases bacterial resistance when overexpressed.
Cryogenic electron microscopy captured FoeAB in open‑inward and open‑outward conformations.
FoeAB was reconstituted in artificial membranes, directly demonstrating fosfomycin transport.
Fosfomycin is added to the list of antibiotics known to be expelled by bacterial efflux pumps.

vicarious_calibration_fengyun3.headline: Vicarious Calibration Boosts Accuracy of Fengyun‑3D/F Ocean Color Data
vicarious_calibration_fengyun3.summary: A new vicarious calibration model dramatically reduces radiometric bias in FY‑3D and FY‑3F MERSI sensors, enabling reliable quantitative ocean color measurements.
highlights: Calibration model corrects biases in FY‑3D and FY‑3F ocean color channels
