Researchers captured a previously unseen “turnover” state in a molybdenum‑containing nitrogenase.
Findings suggest a common ancestral mechanism for nitrogen fixation across all nitrogenase families.

mrna_clumping_prevention.headline: Cells Evolve Codon Strategies to Keep mRNA From Clumping
mrna_clumping_prevention.summary: Researchers show that natural mRNA sequences in bacteria and humans are tuned to reduce sticky interactions, preventing harmful aggregation inside cells.
highlights: Purified E. coli mRNA aggregates in vitro, but native transcripts remain soluble in vivo
Computational redesign of codons increases aggregation propensity, confirming evolutionary pressure
Human abundant mRNAs display the same reduced‑stickiness signature as bacterial transcripts

2609_17315v1.headline: LHAASO Proton Knee Suggests Super‑Heavy Dark Matter but Photon Data Disprove It
2609_17315v1.summary: A relic particle of 5 × 10⁷ GeV could explain LHAASO’s proton hardening at 0.34 PeV and the 3.3 PeV knee, yet its accompanying photons clash with observations.
highlights: Proton spectrum from LHAASO shows a hardening at 0.34 PeV and a knee at 3.3 PeV
A superheavy dark‑matter particle of mass 5 × 10⁷ GeV decaying in the Galactic halo reproduces the proton features
All three hadronic‑interaction‑model reconstructions fit the nucleon‑channel hypothesis
Predicted gamma‑ray cascade exceeds LHAASO diffuse Galactic emission by an order of magnitude
Photon fraction from the model overshoots measured cosmic‑ray photons by two orders of magnitude

2609_16740v1.headline: Nearby Galaxies Show Dark Matter Cores Smaller Than ΛCDM Predictions
2609_16740v1.summary: A study of 136 galaxies from 10^9 to 10^{11.5} M⊙ reveals central dark matter densities far below those expected from ΛCDM simulations.
highlights: Central dark matter densities decline from ~10 kpc in 10^{10} M⊙ galaxies to >50 kpc in 10^{11.5} M⊙ systems
Hydrodynamical simulations invoking baryonic feedback often predict overly steep inner density profiles
The analysis spans radii of 20–50 kpc, providing a comprehensive benchmark across a wide stellar‑mass range

2609_17275v1.headline: Murchison Widefield Array Detects First Unbiased Low‑Frequency Fast Radio Burst
2609_17275v1.summary: A wide‑field imaging survey with the Murchison Widefield Array has captured the first non‑targeted FRB below 300 MHz, confirming a comparable event rate to higher‑frequency detections.
highlights: First FRB detection below 300 MHz from a non‑targeted survey
Imaging‑based search overcomes dispersive delay and scattering challenges
Event rate matches that observed at frequencies above 400 MHz

2609_16394v1.headline: SN 2018ibb’s Light Curve Reveals Dense Circumstellar Matter Around Pair‑Instability Supernova
2609_16394v1.summary: Analysis of SN 2018ibb’s post‑peak light curve shows that interaction with dense circumstellar matter can explain its unexpected blue excess and luminosity break.
highlights: Bolometric luminosity from 150 d after peak matches models with CSM mass‑loss rate 0.01 (v_CSM/1,000 km s⁻¹) M⊙ yr⁻¹
The luminosity break at ~300 d indicates CSM interaction ended, implying a CSM radius of 8.5e16 cm
Progenitor mass loss was enhanced for ~28 (v_CSM/1,000 km s⁻¹)⁻¹ yr before explosion

hotjupiter_ngts10_phasecurve.headline: JWST Reveals Cloud Gaps and Deep Heat Transport on Hot‑Jupiter NGTS‑10 Ab
hotjupiter_ngts10_phasecurve.summary: Using JWST NIRSpec PRISM phase‑curve data, researchers mapped NGTS‑10 Ab’s reflected light and thermal emission, finding anti‑correlated clouds and temperature.
highlights: Thermal emission peaks eastward while reflected light peaks westward, showing distinct atmospheric dynamics
Clouds of micron‑sized silicate particles evaporate over the hottest eastern substellar region
Heat transport efficiency increases with depth, with a measured offset slope of 7.1 ± 1.9 ° per pressure dex

2609_16425v1.headline: Reanalysis Shows 43 GeV Gamma‑Ray Line in Galaxy Clusters Unlikely to Signal Dark Matter
2609_16425v1.summary: A fresh study of Fermi‑LAT data finds the reported 43 GeV line across Virgo, Fornax and Ophiuchus clusters has a broad spatial profile inconsistent with dark‑matter annihilation.
highlights: The excess persists in multiple event‑type partitions and independent data subsets
Uniform surface brightness across the virial region fits the signal better than a central NFW profile
Statistical significance peaks at 2.7 σ after accounting for five morphological models

brown_dwarf_weather.headline: JWST Uncovers Jupiter‑Like Weather Patterns on Brown Dwarf SIMP 0136
brown_dwarf_weather.summary: Using JWST data and principal component analysis, researchers found that SIMP 0136’s atmospheric changes are driven by just two dominant processes.
highlights: Two principal components explain most of the brown dwarf’s brightness variations
The components correspond to temperature shifts and vertical cloud structure changes
Three recurring weather states rotate into view, creating hotter, thinner‑cloud regions and cooler, thicker‑cloud zones

neutron_star_eos.headline: Universal Functional Form Accurately Captures Neutron-Star Equation‑of‑State Across Diverse Models
neutron_star_eos.summary: A new piecewise‑continuous parametrization reproduces tabulated dense‑matter equations of state and matches multimessenger neutron‑star observations with high fidelity.
highlights: Validated against tabulated EoSs from CompOSE and LALSimulation repositories
Bayesian inference using synthetic noise and multimessenger mass‑tidal data constrains parameter correlations
Fits span from very soft to very stiff EoSs, preserving macroscopic neutron‑star observables

2609_16547v1.headline: DESI Spectra Reveal No Optical Absorption from Multi‑State Dark Matter
2609_16547v1.summary: A stacking analysis of 145,087 DESI early‑release spectra finds no optical‑depth signal, setting new limits on magnetic dipole transitions of MeV‑scale dark matter.
highlights: Stacked 145,087 DESI spectra paired with foreground GAMA galaxy groups
Placed 2σ upper limits on magnetic dipole transition cross‑section for ΔE≈3–5 eV
Limits target a few MeV dark matter mass inaccessible to BBN, CMB and direct searches

gw_bias_illustristng300.headline: Machine‑Learned Merger Rates Reveal Stronger Gravitational‑Wave Bias in IllustrisTNG300
gw_bias_illustristng300.summary: A new simulation framework using a machine‑learning emulator calibrated with GALAXYRATE shows BBH mergers preferentially reside in massive, metal‑rich halos, increasing GW bias.
highlights: GW sources exhibit higher bias than the overall galaxy population
The machine‑learned model adds scale‑dependent bias beyond stellar‑mass weighting
Metallicity correlates positively with both GW and galaxy bias

cosmic_noon_miri_wfss.headline: MIRI WFSS Survey of Hubble Ultra Deep Field Reveals 3.3 µm PAH Traces Star Formation at Cosmic Noon
cosmic_noon_miri_wfss.summary: Using JWST's MIRI wide‑field slitless spectroscopy, researchers obtained spectra of 47 galaxies up to redshift 3.712, confirming the 3.3 µm PAH feature as a reliable star‑formation indicator during the Cosmic Noon era.
highlights: Spectra of 47 galaxies with confirmed redshifts were captured using MIRI WFSS in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
The 3.3 µm PAH luminosities correlate tightly with total infrared luminosity and SED‑derived star‑formation rates
Observations cover redshifts 0.67–3.1, fully spanning the peak star‑formation period known as Cosmic Noon

alzheimer_immune_cells.headline: Lymph‑Node Dendritic Cells Trigger Alzheimer’s Damage, Study Finds
alzheimer_immune_cells.summary: Researchers found that suppressing dendritic cells in lymph nodes protects mice from tau‑driven neurodegeneration, suggesting a new peripheral target for Alzheimer’s therapy.
highlights: In mice lacking lymph‑node dendritic cells, brain tau accumulation persisted but neurodegeneration was markedly reduced
Fewer T cells entered the brains of dendritic‑cell‑deficient mice, linking peripheral immune priming to brain inflammation
The study, published in Nature Neuroscience on September 3, used engineered tau‑linked mouse models to test the hypothesis

jwst_gas_outflows_dead_galaxies.headline: Webb Telescope Finds Record‑Breaking Gas Outflows in Distant Dead Galaxies
jwst_gas_outflows_dead_galaxies.summary: Astronomers using JWST/NIRSpec measured the strongest neutral‑gas outflows ever seen from quiescent galaxies 11‑13 billion years ago, yet most of the gas likely falls back.
highlights: Outflows detected in 13 of 23 massive quiescent galaxies at redshift 2.82–4.62
Neutral Na I D absorption reveals outflow rates 10–100 × higher than ionized gas
The most extreme case, galaxy DD‑236, shows a record‑high outflow linked to an active black hole

human_brain_organoid_mice_shrink.headline: Scientists Replace Missing Mouse Brain Tissue with Human Organoids in Groundbreaking Study
human_brain_organoid_mice_shrink.summary: Researchers transplanted human brain organoids into genetically modified mice lacking most of their cortex, achieving 90% integration and functional growth.
highlights: Genetically modified mice develop only 2% of their cerebral cortex and lack much of the hippocampus
Human cortical organoids were injected into the vacant space, integrating successfully in about 90% of cases
Transplanted mice displayed subtle deficits in fine‑motor skills, working memory, and socialization
The study, published in Nature, offers a new platform for modeling neurodevelopmental disorders

mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.institution: University of California, Berkeley (or relevant lab)
mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.headline: UCL researchers reconstruct 10‑second movies from mouse visual‑cortex activity
mouse_brain_visual_reconstruction.summary: Scientists at University College London used calcium imaging of neurons to recreate 10‑second video clips solely from mouse brain signals, revealing how visual input is internally represented.
highlights: Reconstructed videos matched unseen movies using a dynamic neural encoding model
Accuracy improved with data from more individual neurons in the visual cortex
Pixel correlation showed only small timing differences between original and reconstructed clips

240myr_fossil_dinosaur_timeline.headline: Tanzanian Fossil Redefines Timeline of Earliest Dinosaurs
240myr_fossil_dinosaur_timeline.summary: A 240‑million‑year‑old Tanzanian dicynodont named Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda forces scientists to revise the earliest dinosaur timeline by showing the rocks are younger than previously thought.
highlights: Dinodontosaurus isiyavamanda is the first record of the genus outside South America
The specimen, collected in 1963, lay in the Natural History Museum London for over 60 years before identification
Radiometric dating suggests Tanzanian rock layers are up to 10 million years younger than comparable South African deposits
The study was published in the peer‑reviewed Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology on September 15, 2026

chariklo_ring_dynamics.headline: Chariklo’s Rings Show Rapid Opacity Shifts, New JWST Data Reveal
chariklo_ring_dynamics.summary: Observations by the James Webb Space Telescope in 2022 indicate that Chariklo’s inner and outer rings altered their opacity within just a few years.
highlights: Inner ring became significantly more opaque while the outer ring grew clearer
Study led by the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia used stellar occultations to track changes
Findings published in Science Advances challenge assumptions about ring stability on small bodies

prime_assembly_universal_gene_therapies.headline: Prime Assembly Enables Multi‑Mutation Gene Repair, Paving Way for Universal Therapies
prime_assembly_universal_gene_therapies.summary: A new Nature paper shows prime assembly can stitch long DNA fragments into precise genome sites, correcting many mutations with a single approach.
highlights: Prime assembly writes DNA flaps that capture matching gene‑sized fragments for precise insertion
The method avoids double‑strand breaks and works in non‑dividing cells, reducing toxicity
It builds on prime editing, offering a mutation‑agnostic strategy for diseases with hundreds of variants

human_organoid_mice.headline: Stanford Researchers Create Half‑Human Mice Hosting Human Brain Organoids
human_organoid_mice.summary: Scientists at Stanford University engineered mice with half a brain replaced by human cerebral organoids, revealing human pyramidal neurons and large‑scale social‑cognition cells in vivo.
highlights: Neuro‑chimeric mice contain human cerebral organoids grown inside a genetically reduced mouse brain
Human pyramidal projection neurons were detected in the chimeric brains and some migrated into spinal cords
Super‑sized neurons linked to social cognition, previously seen only in elephants, whales and primates, appeared in the mice

jwst_brown_dwarf_class.headline: JWST Uncovers Record‑Low‑Mass Brown Dwarfs in IC 348 Star Cluster
jwst_brown_dwarf_class.summary: A deeper JWST survey of the IC 348 region identified 39 candidates, confirming nine brown dwarfs as light as 2 MJup, redefining the low‑mass limit of star formation.
highlights: 39 new brown‑dwarf candidates were found in IC 348
Spectra of 15 objects revealed nine sub‑stellar members with masses down to ≈2 MJup
All 11 brown dwarfs showing a 3.4 µm aliphatic hydrocarbon feature define a new spectral class H
Two of the faintest objects exhibit circumstellar‑disk excess, hinting at planet‑forming material

baby_planet_elias2_24b.headline: New ‘Baby’ Planet Elias 2‑24 b Sets Record as Youngest Known World
baby_planet_elias2_24b.summary: Astronomers have confirmed that the Jupiter‑mass planet Elias 2‑24 b, less than a million years old, is orbiting a star 450 light‑years away, shattering previous age records.
highlights: Elias 2‑24 b is under one‑million‑year‑old, making it the youngest confirmed exoplanet
The planet was detected in archival coronagraph data from the W. M. Keck Observatory
Its discovery challenges planet‑formation models that predict Jupiter‑size planets need ~5 million years to form

tno_surface_origin.headline: Surface Colors Reveal Origins of Tiny Trans‑Neptunian Objects
tno_surface_origin.summary: New JWST and Hubble observations show that even the smallest TNOs retain surface color signatures that distinguish cold‑origin from hot‑origin bodies.
highlights: Cold TNOs display uniformly reddish surfaces while hot TNOs show a broader color range
The size distributions of hot and cold TNOs are statistically similar, implying comparable collision histories
Fewer small TNOs are observed than predicted by planetary formation models

microbes_adhesive_materials.headline: Engineered E. coli Turns Glucose into High‑Performance Hot‑Melt Adhesives
microbes_adhesive_materials.summary: Researchers at KAIST engineered Escherichia coli to produce aromatic polyhydroxyalkanoate polymers from glucose, achieving adhesive strength surpassing commercial petroleum‑based hot‑melt glues.
highlights: Poly(4HB‑co‑PhLA) reached a lap‑shear strength of 4.58 MPa, exceeding the 4.20 MPa of commercial EVA adhesive
Fed‑batch fermentation yielded up to 52.8 g L⁻¹ of poly(3HB‑co‑4HB‑co‑PhLA)
The polymers retain adhesion after repeated melting, and are enzymatically degradable

2609_18168v1.headline: Varying Higgs VEV May Resolve Primordial Element Discrepancies, Study Finds
2609_18168v1.summary: A 1.58% increase in the Higgs vacuum expectation value during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis aligns helium, deuterium and lithium abundances with observations, but implies non‑standard cosmology.
highlights: A 1.58% uplift of the Higgs VEV during BBN produces agreement with the new primordial 4He measurement by the EMPRESS group.
Deuterium abundance from Lyman‑alpha forest absorption lines and lithium on the Spite plateau are simultaneously matched.
A 0.2% Higgs VEV increase partially eases the cosmic Li problem while remaining consistent with CMB constraints.

arxiv_2609_18552v1.headline: Dark Subhaloes Impart Rotation‑Like Signals in Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxies
arxiv_2609_18552v1.summary: Controlled N‑body simulations show that encounters with dark matter subhaloes generate transient, rotation‑like kinematic features detectable in dwarf spheroidal stellar velocity fields.
highlights: Rotation‑like patterns appear in line‑of‑sight velocities despite initially non‑rotating stellar components
Plane‑of‑sky velocities exhibit alternating expansion, contraction, and opposite streaming directions
Power‑spectrum analysis quantifies spatial scales and strengthens with more massive subhaloes
Recovering the full velocity‑space signature typically requires about O(10^{4}) stellar tracers

2609_18912v1.headline: ZTF Detects First Strongly Lensed Superluminous Supernova SN 2025wny at Record Redshift
2609_18912v1.summary: Astronomers confirm SN 2025wny as the first strongly lensed SLSN‑I, finding its discovery rate aligns with simulations of ZTF’s seven‑year survey.
highlights: SN 2025wny is multiply imaged by two foreground galaxies at zₗ = 0.375
The source lies at zₛ = 2.015, making it the highest‑redshift galaxy‑scale lensed supernova
Simulated ZTF detection rate of 0.037^{+0.022}_{-0.020} yr⁻¹ matches the observed 0.14^{+0.31}_{-0.11} yr⁻¹

z7_cgm_enrichment.headline: Dense Metal‑Rich CGM Absorber Linked to Dust‑Obscured Galaxy at z≈7
z7_cgm_enrichment.summary: Astronomers discovered a dense, metal‑rich circumgalactic absorber at z = 7.03, driven by a heavily dust‑obscured starburst galaxy only visible in long‑wavelength JWST imaging.
highlights: The absorber shows the strongest equivalent widths and column densities recorded beyond redshift 5
Host galaxy ND1 lies just ~16 kpc from the quasar sightline and is detected only in JWST/NIRCam long‑wavelength bands
Outflow rate of 64 M⊙ yr⁻¹ and mass‑loading factor η≈3 indicate a powerful, metal‑laden wind
Enhanced [C/O] ratio hints at nucleosynthesis from Population III supernovae

2609_17665v1.headline: New Bayesian Study Limits Active Galactic Nucleus Contribution to LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA Binary Black Hole Mergers
2609_17665v1.summary: A unified hierarchical analysis of GWTC‑5.0 events and the Quaia AGN catalogue finds that no more than about half of observed mergers can originate from AGN discs.
highlights: Unified likelihood combines spatial correlation and population inference for the AGN fraction $f_{\rm agn}$
Using GWTC‑5.0 and Quaia, the study excludes $f_{\rm agn}\geq0.52$ for AGN with $L_{\rm bol}\ge10^{44.5}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$
Constraints tighten to $f_{\rm agn}\geq0.41$ for $L_{\rm bol}\ge10^{45.5}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $f_{\rm agn}\geq0.61$ for

arxiv_2609_17894v1.headline: Graph Neural Networks Accelerate Disequilibrium Chemistry Modeling for Exoplanet Atmospheres
arxiv_2609_17894v1.summary: A new graph neural network surrogate reduces chemistry computation errors three‑fold, matching JWST and Ariel precision for most simulated exoplanet atmospheres.
highlights: GNN treats chemical species as nodes and temperature‑dependent reaction rates as edges
Mean abundance error drops by ~3× versus prior U‑Net model
Only ~7% of test cases exceed 20 ppm spectral error, within JWST/Ariel limits

youngest_exoplanet_elias.headline: Newborn Jupiter‑Mass Exoplanet Elias 2‑24 b Discovered at 450 Light‑Years
youngest_exoplanet_elias.summary: Astronomers identified Elias 2‑24 b, a Jupiter‑mass planet less than one million years old, orbiting a star 450 light‑years away within its natal debris disk.
highlights: Planet mass comparable to Jupiter despite its extreme youth
Age estimated at under one million years, the youngest known exoplanet
Located 450 light‑years from Earth in a gap of a protoplanetary disk
Discovery made by re‑analyzing archival coronagraph data from the W.M. Keck Observatory

pluto_liquid_nitrogen_flow_evidence.headline: New Horizons Finds Evidence of Liquid Nitrogen Flow on Pluto’s Sputnik Planitia Glacier
pluto_liquid_nitrogen_flow_evidence.summary: Scientists analyzing New Horizons images have identified dark markings that suggest liquid nitrogen may have risen through cracks and wetted Pluto’s frozen surface in recent times.
highlights: Dark features on Sputnik Planitia resemble terrestrial ice‑sheet wetting patterns
Computer models show nitrogen ice can melt at the glacier’s base and rise upward
The study appears in the peer‑reviewed Planetary Science Journal

z7_halo_masses.headline: JADES Uses Galaxy Pairs to Measure Dark Matter Halos at Cosmic Dawn
z7_halo_masses.summary: Using JWST [O III] spectroscopy of ten early‑Universe galaxy pairs, JADES estimates halo masses at z≈7, revealing a high stellar‑to‑halo mass ratio.
highlights: Dynamical mass estimators recover halo masses with ~0.2 dex scatter in the TNG100 simulation
Mean halo mass measured is log⁡(M₍₂₀₀₎/M⊙)=11.06±0.21 for galaxies with log⁡(M/M⊙)=9
Integrated star formation efficiency is 5⁺³₋₂ %, roughly twice the TNG100 prediction

experimental_mesothelioma_drug_targeting.headline: Experimental Drug RSO‑021 Halts Mesothelioma Progression in 67% of Patients
experimental_mesothelioma_drug_targeting.summary: A phase‑one trial of the mitochondrial PRX3 inhibitor RSO‑021 controlled disease in 67% of relapsed mesothelioma patients, showing promising survival benefits.
highlights: Disease progression was halted in 67% of the 15‑patient cohort.
The drug, derived from the antibiotic thiostrepton, targets mitochondrial PRX3.
Average progression‑free survival reached 4.2 months with no drug‑related deaths.
Treatment was delivered locally via chest catheter, minimizing systemic exposure.

2609_18226v1.headline: CTA Could Spot 100 TeV Gamma Rays from Young Supernovae Within 4 Mpc
2609_18226v1.summary: Simulations show dense circumstellar winds enable PeV cosmic‑ray acceleration, producing 100 TeV gamma rays detectable by CTA up to 4 Mpc despite attenuation.
highlights: Kinetic‑MHD models predict CRs reaching ~3 PeV within tens of days after explosion in dense RSG winds.
Photospheric photons reduce intrinsic 1‑100 TeV gamma‑ray flux by roughly a factor of ten.
CTA can detect 100 TeV gamma rays in 50 h exposures out to ~4 Mpc for CSM radius ~3×10¹⁵ cm.
Shrinking CSM to 2×10¹⁵ cm lowers detection horizon to ~3 Mpc.

clues_2_ms_x_ray_point_source_catalog_of.headline: Chandra ULTRADEEP Survey of Abell 2744 Yields 327 X‑ray Point Sources in 2 Ms Exposure
clues_2_ms_x_ray_point_source_catalog_of.summary: The CLUES project presents a 2 Ms Chandra ACIS‑I survey of the Abell 2744 field, detecting 327 X‑ray point sources across 369 arcmin².
highlights: 2 Ms of Chandra ACIS‑I data combined from 101 archival observations
Strong‑lensing magnification by the z = 0.3 Abell 2744 cluster boosts depth
50 % flux completeness reaches 6.3×10⁻¹⁶ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹ (full band)
Catalog includes photometry and basic spectral properties for 327 sources

dust_decrease_climate_warming.headline: Atmospheric Dust Decline by 10% May Accelerate Global Warming
dust_decrease_climate_warming.summary: A UCLA‑led study finds atmospheric dust fell 10% between 2003 and 2023, potentially amplifying human‑driven warming due to dust’s cooling effect.
highlights: Dust in the atmosphere dropped about 10% from 2003 to 2023
The decline reverses a century‑long increase that peaked in the 1980s
Dust’s modest cooling effect means its loss can add to recent warming

youngest_planet_discovery.headline: Youngest Known Exoplanet Discovered Orbiting Distant Star Elias 2‑24 b
youngest_planet_discovery.summary: Astronomers have confirmed a Jupiter‑mass planet less than one million years old, offering a rare glimpse of a giant planet still forming within its dusty disk.
highlights: Elias 2‑24 b is roughly Jupiter‑size and orbits a star about 450 light‑years from Earth.
The planet was identified using Keck Observatory’s coronagraph on archived NASA data.
Its age under one million years challenges standard giant‑planet formation models that predict several‑million‑year timescales.
Future observations with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope could reveal many more infant planets.

fossil_mission_proposal.headline: FOSSIL Mission Aims to Measure CMB Spectral Distortions with Unprecedented Sensitivity
fossil_mission_proposal.summary: The proposed FOSSIL space telescope will map sky intensity from 50 GHz to 2 THz, achieving three‑order‑of‑magnitude improvement over COBE/FIRAS for mu‑type, y‑type and relativistic y‑type distortions.
highlights: FOSSIL targets absolute spectroscopic precision across 130 channels spanning 50 GHz–2 THz
Sensitivity gains of ~10³ over COBE/FIRAS enable detection of tiny mu‑type and y‑type CMB distortions
Measurements will constrain primordial density fluctuations at k≈10–10⁴ Mpc⁻¹ and test inflationary scenarios
Data will probe dark‑matter annihilation, primordial black‑hole seeds, and cosmic thermal energy budget
Legacy science includes detailed Cosmic Infrared Background characterization and Galactic dust mapping

jwst_little_red_dots_black_holes.headline: JWST’s Little Red Dots May Be Rapidly Growing Early Black Holes
jwst_little_red_dots_black_holes.summary: New supercomputer simulations suggest the tiny, intensely red objects seen by JWST are black‑hole seeds that grew dozens of times faster than today’s black holes, potentially solving the early‑Universe black‑hole mystery.
highlights: Simulations on Japan’s ATERUI III supercomputer reproduce the observed properties of Little Red Dots
Intense far‑ultraviolet radiation suppresses normal star formation, allowing a supermassive star to collapse into a black‑hole
Dense gas disks trap radiation, enabling black holes to accrete at rates far exceeding modern limits

brain_structure_pearl.headline: Pearled Axons Reveal Hidden Structure Challenging a Century‑Old Textbook View
brain_structure_pearl.summary: Researchers using high‑pressure freezing electron microscopy found that mouse and human axons form string‑of‑pearls morphologies that alter signal speed.
highlights: Axons display nanoscale “non‑synaptic varicosities” resembling pearls rather than smooth tubes.
Increasing membrane tension or cholesterol removal reduces pearl size and slows electrical conduction.
High‑frequency stimulation expands pearls by up to 17%, prolonging signal slowdown for over an hour.
Pearled axons were also observed in human cortical tissue from epilepsy surgeries.

temperature_measurement_error_impact.headline: Temperature Proxy Errors May Understate Climate Impacts by 15%
temperature_measurement_error_impact.summary: A new study shows that measurement errors in temperature proxies can cause climate‑impact estimates to undervalue effects by at least fifteen percent.
highlights: Microclimate blind spots cause errors up to nearly 15 °F in mountainous regions like Boulder, Colorado
Average proxy error of 3.3 °F (1.85 °C) exceeds the Paris Agreement warming limit of 1.5 °C
Using over 20 million crime records, coarser geographic aggregation reduced estimated heat‑related crime impacts

rare_lung_cancer_mutation_nonsmokers.headline: Rare EGFR T790M Mutation Raises Lung Cancer Risk 62‑Fold in Nonsmokers
rare_lung_cancer_mutation_nonsmokers.summary: A study of over 3 million people finds the inherited EGFR T790M variant makes nonsmokers 62 times more likely to develop lung cancer than non‑carriers.
highlights: The EGFR T790M mutation appears in 1 in 15,850 individuals of European ancestry
Carriers have about 25‑times the odds of lung cancer overall, regardless of smoking status
The variant is especially common in the Southeast US, with 1 in 2,078 carriers in Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee

quantum_jump_sound_observation.headline: Stanford Researchers Observe Real‑Time Quantum Jumps of Sound in Microscopic Resonator
quantum_jump_sound_observation.summary: A Stanford team directly recorded phonon quantum jumps in a chip‑scale mechanical resonator, marking the first real‑time observation of sound behaving quantum mechanically.
highlights: Quantum jumps of sound were captured by pairing a microscopic mechanical resonator with a superconducting qubit
The resonator’s two‑millisecond ringdown allowed hundreds of readouts to pinpoint the transition from one phonon state to zero
The technique offers a new pathway for quantum error correction and ultra‑precise sensing of biological molecules

european_ash_pangenome_naturecomm.institution: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew & Forest Research
european_ash_pangenome_naturecomm.headline: European ash pangenome unlocks genes for breeding ash‑dieback‑resistant trees
european_ash_pangenome_naturecomm.summary: A new European ash pangenome built from 50 diverse trees reveals 211 candidate resistance genes, offering a roadmap to breed disease‑resilient forests.
highlights: First‑ever European ash (Fraxinus excelsior) pangenome assembled from 50 trees
Analysis of >1,000 trees identified 211 genes linked to ash dieback resistance
16 of those genes are dispensable, present only in some individuals
Pangenome is 22% larger than a single‑tree reference, adding >3,400 dispensable genes (9% of total)
Study published in Nature Communications, a peer‑reviewed article

rare_variant_never_smoker_lung_cancer.headline: Rare Genetic Variant Raises Lung Cancer Risk 25‑Fold in Never‑Smokers
rare_variant_never_smoker_lung_cancer.summary: A rare genetic variant linked to a 25‑fold increase in lung cancer odds among never‑smokers was identified using 23andMe data.
highlights: The variant confers roughly 25‑times higher odds of developing lung cancer.
It is especially prevalent in Southern Appalachia compared with other U.S. regions.
The discovery was made by analyzing genetic data from millions of 23andMe participants.
The finding appears in the peer‑reviewed journal Science.
Researchers caution the variant explains only a small fraction of never‑smoker cases.

handheld_mid_ir_spectrometer.headline: Handheld Mid‑Infrared Scanner Matches Lab‑scale Imaging Quality
handheld_mid_ir_spectrometer.summary: A compact handheld MIRSI device, developed at the University of Houston, delivers chemical composition maps with resolution and accuracy comparable to conventional benchtopsized systems.
highlights: Handheld probe measures 8 × 8 in (20 × 20 cm) and uses chalcogenide fibers and mirrors to combine visible and mid‑IR beams.
Achieves 2 µm spatial resolution, five times finer than direct IR detection, with spectral similarity of 0.935 to FTIR references.
Chemical image correlation with a state‑of‑the‑art benchtop system reaches r = 0.90 across cervical and ovarian cancer tissues.

satellite_forest_monitoring_australia.headline: Satellite‑Enabled Sensors to Track Australia’s Forest Health in Near‑Real Time
satellite_forest_monitoring_australia.summary: Researchers are upgrading thousands of solar‑powered sensors to transmit soil moisture and plant stress data via low‑Earth‑orbit satellites across Australia’s diverse forests.
highlights: Western Sydney University and UNSW are piloting satellite‑linked sensors in the Blue Mountains and mulga woodlands of western NSW
Low‑Earth‑orbit communications from OQ Technology will allow continuous data flow from remote sites lacking mobile coverage
The project aims to expand from a demonstration plot to a national network, improving drought and fire risk forecasts

2609_19459v1.headline: JWST Finds Three Fe‑rich Quasars at Cosmic Dawn (z > 6)
2609_19459v1.summary: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations reveal three quasars with exceptionally strong FeII emission, indicating rapid chemical enrichment within the first billion years after the Big Bang.
highlights: FeII strength ratios (R_FeII) of 2.5‑3.6 place the objects in the top ~3% of SDSS quasars
Black‑hole masses span ~0.2‑7×10⁹ M⊙ with Eddington ratios from ~0.1 to 6
One source shows a distinct 1.5 kpc emission‑line region, hinting at a companion galaxy or ionized gas

2609_19295v1.headline: Diffusion Model Reconstructs Projected Dark Matter Map from SDSS Galaxies
2609_19295v1.summary: A conditional diffusion model trained on CAMELS reproduces the projected dark matter density field across 0.1‑100 Mpc scales using SDSS galaxy data.
highlights: Model validated on independent IllustrisTNG300‑1 simulation with <0.2 dex halo‑mass scatter
Typical surface‑density scatter ~0.3 dex on 100 kpc scales
Publicly released 90×90 (h⁻¹ Mpc)² map with 0.097 h⁻¹ Mpc pixel size
Reconstructed field matches SDSS group‑catalog masses and halo‑mass function

2609_19296v1.headline: New CMB‑ACT and SPT Data Sharpen Constraints on Starobinsky Inflation Model
2609_19296v1.summary: Using the latest ACT, SPT, and DESI BAO observations, researchers directly solved the inflation equations, tightening parameter limits beyond traditional slow‑roll estimates.
highlights: Starobinsky inflation parameters constrained more tightly than under the ΛCDM slow‑roll approximation
Reheating temperature limits derived from the global analysis
Correlation between model parameters and the BAO quantity r_d h examined

2609_19788v1.headline: Dual‑Spacecraft Study Finds Widespread Plasma Jets Across Mars’ Magnetosheath
2609_19788v1.summary: Using MAVEN and Tianwen‑1 data, researchers show that high‑pressure plasma jets permeate the Martian magnetosheath, unlike the localized jets seen at Earth.
highlights: Plasma jets appear throughout the entire Martian magnetosheath
Jets are linked to Mars’ extended hydrogen corona generating pickup ions
Upstream proton‑cyclotron waves appear to drive jet formation
Finding applies to any body with an exosphere, including unmagnetized exoplanets

2609_20021v1.headline: JWST Unveils Little Red Dots: Transient SIDM‑Driven Black Hole Growth Phase
2609_20021v1.summary: A new model links compact red galaxies seen by JWST to a brief epoch where self‑interacting dark matter fuels rapid black‑hole growth within dense nuclear disks.
highlights: JWST identified a population of compact, red galaxies with broad emission lines and weak X‑ray output, dubbed Little Red Dots
Gas inflows create a nuclear thick disk that reshapes the central SIDM distribution, enabling rapid SIDM accretion onto seed
SIDM‑driven accretion produces the characteristic V‑shaped spectral energy distribution and suppresses short‑wavelength
The model predicts LRDs appear during strong nuclear inflow and evolve into typical AGN after the SIDM episode, offering a

metal_poor_eclipsing_binaries.headline: Metal-Poor Eclipsing Binaries Yield Precise Masses and Radii
metal_poor_eclipsing_binaries.summary: Using TESS photometry and spectra from PEPSI, Levy, and CHIRON, researchers measured masses and radii of thirty metal‑poor stars with sub‑1% uncertainties.
highlights: Three binaries have [M/H] < ‑2.0, including J0001+2156 at [M/H] = ‑2.51, the most metal‑poor system known
Median fractional uncertainties in mass and radius are below 1 % across the sample
Ages derived from isochrone fitting reach up to 13.8⁺⁰·⁸₋⁰·⁷ Gyr, confirming ancient halo origins

crispr_ancestor.headline: Ancient Viral VIPR System Uncovered as Possible Precursor to CRISPR Gene‑Editing
crispr_ancestor.summary: Two new Science papers reveal a virus‑derived RNA‑guided defense, VIPR, that may have seeded bacterial CRISPR systems and could broaden genome‑editing tools.
highlights: VIPR proteins and vrRNA were identified in bacterial and viral genomes using structure‑based searches
VIPR employs a unique “skip‑one” code, forming a three‑stranded RNA‑DNA‑protein triplex
Reprogrammed VIPR silenced genes and protected E. coli from phage infection in laboratory tests

graph_sandwich_proof.headline: Mathematicians Resolve Long‑Standing Graph Sandwich Conjecture
graph_sandwich_proof.summary: A trio from Warwick proved the graph sandwich conjecture, linking random regular and binomial graphs and unlocking new proofs for complex networks.
highlights: The conjecture, posed in 2004, claimed any large enough regular graph can be sandwiched between two binomial graphs
Richard Montgomery, Natalie Behague, and Daniel Iľkovič completed the proof in 2025 using an edge‑by‑edge construction
The result lets researchers transfer properties from well‑studied binomial graphs to harder regular graphs instantly

cells_cheat_death_rebuild_tissue.headline: Weizmann Scientists Identify Death-Resistant Cells That Drive Tissue Regeneration
cells_cheat_death_rebuild_tissue.summary: Researchers discovered DARE cells that activate initiator caspases, survive apoptosis, and rapidly rebuild damaged epithelial tissue, while their descendants gain heightened resistance.
highlights: DARE cells activate initiator caspase Dronc but halt before executioner caspases, allowing survival after ionizing radiation
NARE cells lack initiator caspase activation yet cooperate with DARE cells via a negative‑feedback loop
Descendants of DARE cells become up to seven‑fold more resistant to subsequent cell‑death insults

einstein_gravity_muonium_beam.headline: ETH Zurich and PSI Prepare First Gravity Test with Exotic Muonium Beam
einstein_gravity_muonium_beam.summary: Researchers have created a cold muonium beam using superfluid helium, enabling the first measurement of how second‑generation particles respond to Earth’s gravity.
highlights: Cold muonium atoms are produced in superfluid helium near absolute zero
The beam’s uniform speed allows an interferometer to detect tiny gravitational shifts
Testing the equivalence principle on a second‑generation particle could reveal new forces

human_brain_two_distinct_origins.headline: Human Brain Originates from Two Distinct Embryonic Progenitor Systems
human_brain_two_distinct_origins.summary: A Stanford-led study published in Nature Neuroscience shows that forebrain‑midbrain and hindbrain arise from separate progenitor cells during early gastrulation.
highlights: Forebrain and midbrain progenitors express the gene Otx2
Hindbrain progenitors express the gene Gbx2 and can be driven to form functional motor neurons
The dual‑system pattern is conserved in mouse, macaque, chicken, zebrafish and acorn worm embryos

toi_1355b_discovery_pasj.headline: Hot Jupiter TOI-1355 b’s Eccentric Orbit Will Vanish From View After 2033
toi_1355b_discovery_pasj.summary: A newly discovered hot Jupiter orbiting the ultra‑hot star TOI‑1355 in a two‑day, highly eccentric path will cease transiting Earth by 2033, limiting further study.
highlights: TOI‑1355 b completes an orbit in about two Earth days
Its orbit is highly eccentric around a star at 8,400 °C
Transit visibility ends around 2033, halting direct observations
Discovery published in Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

xrism_pulsar_wind.headline: XRISM Captures Stellar Wind Feeding Pulsar GX 301‑2 in BP Crucis
xrism_pulsar_wind.summary: Using XRISM’s Resolve spectrometer, astronomers observed ionized iron redshifted as a 335,000 mph wind streams onto neutron star GX 301‑2, powering X‑ray flares.
highlights: XRISM observed BP Crucis for 16 hours on Feb 1 2025, capturing high‑resolution X‑ray spectra.
Iron absorption lines showed a redshift indicating plasma moving toward GX 301‑2 at ~335,000 mph.
The wind‑fed accretion creates turbulent disks that generate multi‑day X‑ray flares during the pulsar’s 41.5‑day orbit.
Findings published in Science Advances, confirming the first direct detection of stellar wind capture by a compact object.

stacked_2d_materials_multiferroicity.headline: Room‑temperature multiferroic 2D heterostructure enables voltage‑controlled magnetism
stacked_2d_materials_multiferroicity.summary: Researchers created a van der Waals Fe₃GaTe₂/CuInP₂S₆ heterostructure that shows multiferroicity at 292 K and allows magnetic switching with small voltages.
highlights: Multiferroic behavior observed at 292 K (≈19 °C) in a stacked Fe₃GaTe₂/CuInP₂S₆ device
Applying ≤ few‑volt bias changes magnetic coercivity, persisting after voltage removal
The magnetic state can be toggled over 3,000 cycles without fatigue

human_evolution_alz_gene.headline: Human Evolution May Be Selecting Against APOE ε4 Variant Linked to Alzheimer’s
human_evolution_alz_gene.summary: A study of 57,696 Europeans shows the frequency of the APOE ε4 risk allele drops after age 70, suggesting it reduces survival to old age.
highlights: APOE ε4 frequency declines among individuals older than about 70 years
The effect was observed in the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohort
A smoking‑related variant near CHRNA3 is linked to shorter paternal lifespans in UK Biobank data

8.headline: Solar System Chose Fire: Early Planetesimals Dominated by Chondrules Over Ice‑Rich Matrix
8.summary: New Yale‑led research shows that within the first million years, nascent planetesimals were composed of 83%‑92% chondrules, with matrix making up only 8%‑17%.
highlights: Early bodies in the outer solar system were 83%‑92% chondrules, far exceeding later‑forming objects
Chemical tracers sulfur and iron oxidation state reveal matrix fractions as low as 8%‑17%
The study, published in Nature Astronomy, provides the first geochemical evidence of preferential chondrule sorting from the

cysteine_toxicity_mechanism.headline: Cysteine Overload Triggers Iron Release from Ferritin, Killing Mitochondria
cysteine_toxicity_mechanism.summary: Excess cysteine pulls iron out of ferritin, floods mitochondria via SLC25A28, and induces iron‑dependent cell death, explaining why cells sequester cysteine into glutathione.
highlights: Cysteine directly reacts with ferritin iron, liberating it into the cytosol
The iron transporter SLC25A28 shuttles the released iron into mitochondria
Blocking ferritin iron release or SLC25A28 prevents cysteine‑induced toxicity

black_hole_merger_explanation.headline: Gravitational Lensing May Explain ‘Impossible’ Black Hole Merger GW231123
black_hole_merger_explanation.summary: A new theoretical study suggests that gravitational lensing amplified the GW231123 signal, reducing the inferred black‑hole masses and resolving the mass‑gap puzzle.
highlights: GW231123 was detected by LIGO on Nov. 23 2023, appearing to involve 100‑ and 130‑solar‑mass black holes.
Researchers propose a lensing object of 190–850 solar masses could have magnified the signal.
Revised modeling lowers the merged black hole’s mass to ~140 solar masses, removing it from the mass gap.
If confirmed, this would be the first observation of gravitational‑wave lensing, opening new ways to probe distant mergers and

y_chromosome_loss_cancer_risk.headline: Loss of Y Chromosome May Signal Early Cancer Development in Men
y_chromosome_loss_cancer_risk.summary: A new study of 1,000 tissue samples shows that loss of the Y chromosome in normal tissue creates a preneoplastic field, indicating early cancer risk.
highlights: Loss of Y chromosome was detected in normal‑appearing tissue adjacent to tumors across 11 major organs
Analysis covered 1,000 samples from 405 men, examining over 4.3 million cell nuclei
Highest Y loss observed in colon, rectum, esophagus, pancreas, and lung cancers

solar_cycle_connection_universetoday_202.headline: Sun’s Sharp Cutoff Point May Forecast Weaker Cycle 26
solar_cycle_connection_universetoday_202.summary: A new analysis by Sandra Chapman finds that the sunspot drop at a solar maximum’s cutoff predicts the strength of the next cycle, suggesting Cycle 26 could be weaker than Cycle 25.
highlights: Sharp decline in sunspot numbers marks a cutoff point at solar maximum
Cutoff sunspot count correlates with the amplitude of the following solar cycle
Current Cycle 25 peaked around 2022 and will decline until ~2030
Chapman predicts Cycle 26 will be weaker, with a testable point in 2028

dna_computer_drop_of_water.headline: DNA‑Powered Computer Solves Calculations in a Drop of Water
dna_computer_drop_of_water.summary: Researchers at Maynooth University built a DNA‑based computer that solves arithmetic problems in a tiny droplet using thermodynamically driven strand interactions.
highlights: The Scaffolded DNA Computer (SDC) performed 10 programs, including 100‑bit calculations, in about 30 seconds per simple sum
Over 700 computations were demonstrated, with larger tasks taking up to 14 hours
The system uses billions to trillions of DNA strands that compete to reach an energetically favored state encoding the answer
The DNA computer is reusable, allowing the same strands to be re‑hydrated and run again after months

exosome_tbi.headline: Cerebral Endothelial Cell Exosomes Home to TBI Lesions and Restore Energy
exosome_tbi.summary: Researchers show that CEC‑derived exosomes use SDF‑1α/CXCR4 signaling to target traumatic brain injury sites and shift glucose metabolism toward oxidative phosphorylation, rescuing ATP levels.
highlights: CEC‑Exos inherit SDF‑1α/CXCR4‑mediated homing, which is lost after siCXCR4 knock‑down
miR‑16‑5p in exosomes redirects metabolism from glycolysis to mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
In mouse TBI models, CEC‑Exos reduce lesion volume, neuronal apoptosis and improve neurological scores

early_jurassic_hyperthermal.headline: Magmatic Carbon Release Fueled Early Jurassic Toarcian Hyperthermal
early_jurassic_hyperthermal.summary: Around 183 million years ago, ~18,000 Pg C of mainly magmatic carbon erupted, driving the Toarcian Oceanic Anoxic Event and a rapid climate spike.
highlights: ~18,000 Pg C of predominantly magmatic carbon released during the T‑OAE
At least 6,800 Pg C of organic carbon buried, aiding climate recovery
Silicate weathering consumed ~6,000 Pg C, further stabilising temperatures

adora1_inhibition_suppresses_colon_cance.headline: Caffeine Blocks ADORA1 to Activate Hippo Pathway and Halt Colon Cancer Growth
adora1_inhibition_suppresses_colon_cance.summary: Researchers show that caffeine competitively inhibits ADORA1, triggering Hippo/YAP signaling and suppressing colon tumor development in pre‑clinical models.
highlights: Caffeine competitively blocks ADORA1 activation, leading to YAP phosphorylation via the Gαi‑cAMP/PKA‑LATS axis
The study uncovers a positive feedback loop where YAP drives ADORA1 transcription, amplifying Hippo signaling
Experiments in mouse colon cancer models demonstrate reduced tumor incidence and progression upon ADORA1 inhibition

gamma_ray_burst_2gly.headline: Brightest Gamma‑Ray Burst Ever Recorded Hits Earth, Disturbs Ionosphere
gamma_ray_burst_2gly.summary: On 9 October 2022 a gamma‑ray burst from a star 2 billion light‑years away struck Earth, producing a measurable ionospheric disturbance detected by multiple satellites.
highlights: GRB 221009A delivered the strongest gamma‑ray burst ever measured, lasting 800 seconds
Integral’s IBIS instrument and the China Seismo‑Electromagnetic Satellite recorded ionospheric electric‑field variations
The event is statistically expected only once every 10,000 years on Earth
Researchers suggest such bursts could have contributed to past mass‑extinction events

alphamissense.headline: AlphaMissense Predicts Pathogenicity for 89% of Human Missense Variants Using AlphaFold‑Derived Structure
alphamissense.summary: A new deep‑learning model, AlphaMissense, leverages AlphaFold2 and population frequency data to classify most human missense variants as likely benign or pathogenic with 90% precision.
highlights: AlphaMissense fine‑tunes AlphaFold on human and primate variant frequency data
The model classifies 32% of variants as likely pathogenic and 57% as likely benign
Predictions for every possible single‑amino‑acid substitution in the human proteome are released as a community resource

new_tiger_cat_species.headline: New South American tiger cat species Leopardus tilcayo identified in Bolivia’s Yungas
new_tiger_cat_species.summary: Researchers used whole‑genome data from 38 tiger cats to reveal five distinct species and formally describe the new species Leopardus tilcayo.
highlights: Leopardus tilcayo diverged from its relatives about 1.4 million years ago
The study, published in Current Biology (Sept 17 2026), used DNA from museum specimens and field samples
Five genetically distinct tiger‑cat species are now recognized across Central and South America

malaria_parasite_stress_transmission_mec.headline: Malaria Parasite Triggers Gametocyte Surge via GDV1 Feedback Under Stress
malaria_parasite_stress_transmission_mec.summary: Plasmodium falciparum senses fever, nutrient loss or DHA exposure and activates a GDV1‑AP2‑HS pathway that rapidly boosts gametocyte production for transmission.
highlights: Nutrient limitation, DHA treatment, and simulated fever all trigger the same GDV1‑AP2‑HS regulatory cascade.
Deleting ap2‑hs abolishes stress‑induced gametocyte formation, confirming its central role.
GDV1 induces gametocytes while gdv1‑as RNA provides a feedback brake to limit GDV1 activity.

global_population_dataset.headline: AI‑Powered LandScan Mosaic Maps Global Daily Population with Uncertainty
global_population_dataset.summary: Researchers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory released LandScan Mosaic, a high‑resolution dataset that models building use to reveal daily human movement worldwide.
highlights: AI estimates building height, floor count, and use type where data are sparse
Provides explicit uncertainty metrics for each population estimate
Tracks ambient population across a full 24‑hour cycle
Improves disaster response, infrastructure planning, and security applications

environment_of_first_supermassive_black_.headline: JWST Reveals Birth Environments of Early Supermassive Black Hole Seeds
environment_of_first_supermassive_black_.summary: Using high‑resolution simulations, researchers identified dark‑matter mergers and cosmic overdensities as the key settings where direct‑collapse black holes first formed less than 500 million years after the Big Bang.
highlights: Dark‑matter merger trees traced the spatial distribution of potential DCBH host haloes
Simulations with GIZMO and the Cosmic Archaeology Tool showed seed formation as early as 13.64 billion years ago
Metal enrichment from Population III supernovae halted direct‑collapse episodes around 13.4 billion years ago

mars_phobos_crater.headline: Giant Stickney Crater May Unlock Phobos’ Origin Mystery
mars_phobos_crater.summary: Researchers model a dense mass beneath Stickney Crater on Phobos, aiming to distinguish between captured‑asteroid and impact‑debris formation scenarios before Japan’s MMX mission returns samples.
highlights: Stickney Crater, 9 km wide, could host a compressed core that alters Phobos’ gravity signal
The study contrasts a 4.2 billion‑year‑old impact‑debris origin with a 2.6 billion‑year‑old captured‑asteroid scenario
MMX, launching late 2026, will sample Phobos’ surface and may confirm interior density predictions

new_human_blood_group.headline: Scientists Identify MAL Gene, Creating New Human Blood Group System
new_human_blood_group.summary: Researchers pinpointed the MAL gene as the source of the long‑standing AnWj antigen, establishing the MAL blood group and enabling genetic donor screening.
highlights: Whole‑exome sequencing linked homozygous MAL deletions to AnWj‑negative phenotype.
Laboratory re‑introduction of MAL restored AnWj antigen expression on cells.
ISBT officially recognized MAL as blood group system ISBT 047, the 47th system.
New genotyping tests can now identify rare AnWj‑negative donors for transfusion safety.

two_color_light_graphene_topology.headline: Two‑color laser pulses steer electrons in graphene’s Floquet topological state
two_color_light_graphene_topology.summary: Researchers used a 1,550‑nm circularly polarized pulse and its 775‑nm second harmonic to dynamically control photocurrents in graphene, revealing valley‑polarized and Hall effects.
highlights: Circularly polarized 1,550‑nm pulses temporarily reshape graphene’s band structure into a Floquet topological insulator
A second‑harmonic 775‑nm field directs electrons, producing photocurrent circular dichroism and an all‑optical anomalous Hall
Measurements show valley‑polarized currents and sub‑cycle sensitivity, confirming control of the transient state

climate_super_pollutant_from_chinas_elec.headline: China’s SF6 Emissions Threaten Climate Gains as Grid Recycling Stalls
climate_super_pollutant_from_chinas_elec.summary: China’s electric grid released about 5,100 metric tons of sulfur hexafluoride in 2021, a potent greenhouse gas that could be cut by 1,400 metric tons annually with modest investment.
highlights: SF6 is 24,300 times more effective than CO₂ at warming the planet and persists for roughly 1,000 years.
Current recycling rates hover around 30 percent, far below the Ministry of Ecology and Environment’s 90 percent target.
Increasing recycling by 1,400 metric tons would cost roughly $6 million per year, less than 0.01 percent of China’s $70 billion
China accounts for more than half of global SF6 emissions, with releases nearly doubling from 2011 to 2021.

einsteins_spooky_action_survives_extreme.headline: Einstein’s ‘spooky action’ survives in fleeting Z‑boson pairs at the LHC
einsteins_spooky_action_survives_extreme.summary: Physicists at the University of Oxford have found strong evidence that Z bosons from Higgs decays remain quantum‑entangled even in the extreme environment of CERN’s Large Hadron Collider.
highlights: Entanglement observed between two heavy, short‑lived Z bosons produced in Higgs boson decays
Analysis of decay‑product angles reconstructed the original Z‑boson spins, revealing quantum correlations
Result published in Physical Review Letters, marking one of the highest‑energy entanglement confirmations

streptococcus_pneumoniae_gene_rewiring.headline: Independent gene modules map transcriptional rewiring in antibiotic‑adapted Streptococcus pneumoniae
streptococcus_pneumoniae_gene_rewiring.summary: Using independent component analysis on 718 RNA‑seq datasets, researchers identified 60 iModulons that differentiate antibiotic‑induced and adaptation‑associated transcriptional responses in the TIG 4 strain.
highlights: 60 iModulons were uncovered, with half overlapping known regulons
The CiaRH iModulon responded to vancomycin in both TIG 4 and serotype 19F strains
Most iModulon activities differed between TIG 4 and serotype 19F, limiting cross‑strain generalisation

dynamics_informed_ml_missing_systems.headline: Dynamics‑Informed Machine Learning Reconstructs Missing High‑Dimensional System Data
dynamics_informed_ml_missing_systems.summary: A new dynamics‑informed imputation framework, Full‑Partial Reconstruction Mapping, accurately fills extensive gaps in high‑dimensional time series across ecology, climate, finance and neuroscience.
highlights: FPRM embeds state‑space dynamical priors and learns diffeomorphic mappings between complete and incomplete attractors.
It successfully imputes up to 90% missing variables in a 120‑dimensional Lorenz system using only one fully observed variable.
Benchmarks on real datasets—road occupancy, EEG, exchange rates, and wind speed—show superior performance to traditional

ice_loss_12trillion_tons_1979_2026.headline: Earth Lost Over 12 Trillion Tons of Ice from Greenland and Antarctica Since 1979
ice_loss_12trillion_tons_1979_2026.summary: Satellite data reveal that 12.5 trillion tons of ice have vanished from Greenland and Antarctica in 47 years, raising sea levels by about an inch.
highlights: 12.5 trillion tons of ice melted from the two ice sheets since 1979
The melt contributed roughly 3 quadrillion gallons of water, lifting global sea level by 3.1 cm
Warmer ocean waters, not just air, drove five‑sixths of the ice loss
Jakobshavn glacier now retreats up to 164 feet (50 m) per day
NASA and ESA satellites enabled the longest‑running ice‑mass record to date

spleen_circulating_cam2_myelofibrosis.headline: Splenectomy Halts Vertebral Osteosclerosis in G6b‑B Deficient Mice via ICAM2 Modulation
spleen_circulating_cam2_myelofibrosis.summary: Removing the spleen in Mpig6b‑deficient female mice prevents vertebral bone overgrowth by lowering circulating ICAM2, while long‑bone osteosclerosis remains unchanged.
highlights: Splenectomy restored platelet counts but did not reverse femoral osteosclerosis in Mpig6b‑/‑ mice
Vertebral bone volume/tissue volume fell significantly after splenectomy, indicating halted osteosclerosis
Plasma proteomics identified soluble ICAM2 as elevated in Mpig6b‑/‑ mice and normalized by splenectomy
Recombinant ICAM2 inhibited osteoclast fusion in vitro, suggesting a mechanistic link to bone loss

mapk_ugt_neonicotinoid_resistance.headline: MAPK pathway activates HR39 to boost UGT‑mediated neonicotinoid resistance in whitefly
mapk_ugt_neonicotinoid_resistance.summary: Elevated UDP‑glycosyltransferase BtUGT356B1 expression, driven by MAPK‑phosphorylated HR39, enhances Bemisia tabaci detoxification of thiamethoxam and imidacloprid.
highlights: P38/ERK kinases phosphorylate transcription factor HR39
HR39 binds the promoter of BtUGT356B1, up‑regulating its transcription
BtUGT356B1 directly metabolises thiamethoxam and imidacloprid

hurricane_hunter_intensification_signs.headline: Hurricane Hunters Identify Four Signs a Tilted Storm Will Strengthen
hurricane_hunter_intensification_signs.summary: Nearly three decades of NOAA Hurricane Hunter data reveal four features that signal a tilted tropical cyclone is aligning vertically and primed for rapid intensification.
highlights: Compact low‑level circulation with strong winds
Favorable tilt relative to vertical wind shear
Intense rising air and heavy rain near the storm’s core
Warm sea surface, abundant moisture, and weak mid‑level winds

ancient_dna_plague_return.headline: Ancient DNA Maps Plague’s Four‑Century Return After the Black Death
ancient_dna_plague_return.summary: Researchers reconstructed 26 Yersinia pestis genomes, revealing repeated introductions and new lineages that kept plague circulating across Europe for over four centuries.
highlights: 26 ancient plague genomes were sequenced from sites in Estonia, Russia, England, the Netherlands and Switzerland
A new phylochronology method narrowed dating windows, linking genomes to specific historical outbreaks
Genetic evidence ties major plague expansions to the Great Renaissance Drought and to wars such as the Thirty Years' War and the

ultra_bright_nanoparticles_2026.headline: University of Toronto Nanoparticles Turn Infrared Light Into Bright Green Signals
ultra_bright_nanoparticles_2026.summary: Researchers created dye‑sensitized upconversion nanoparticles that emit green light 150‑times brighter, enabling detection of trace chemicals and discrimination of near‑identical molecular isomers.
highlights: Upconversion particles absorb low‑energy near‑infrared photons and emit high‑energy green light
A layered LiLuF4 core‑shell‑shell design packs more ytterbium ions while preventing back‑energy transfer
Sensitivity allows detection of impurities as low as 10% structural isomer in drug batches

synthetic_secretion_switches_2026.headline: Unconventional Protein Secretion Offers Faster Switches for Engineered Mammalian Cells
synthetic_secretion_switches_2026.summary: A review highlights how bypassing the ER‑Golgi route could accelerate synthetic secretion switches, reducing latency from hours to minutes.
highlights: Current rapid secretion switches still rely on the classical ER‑Golgi pathway, limiting speed
Unconventional secretion mechanisms such as membrane translocation and extracellular vesicles remain largely untapped
Designing switches at terminal export steps could cut response times to minutes
Key bottlenecks include basal leakage, cargo compatibility, and lack of modular interfaces

roman_telescope_first_image_2026.headline: Roman Telescope’s First Test Image Shows Neon‑Green Stars
roman_telescope_first_image_2026.summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope captured a neon‑green star field in its inaugural 300‑megapixel test image, confirming the Wide Field Instrument is operational.
highlights: Hundreds of stars appear as lime‑colored loops because the Wide Field Instrument is still being focused
The 18 detectors in the camera will eventually deliver up to 1.4 terabytes of data per day
Roman will survey galaxies to probe dark energy and use its coronagraph to study exoplanets, potentially raising known worlds

hidden_gut_defect_ibd.headline: Hidden gut defect may explain recurring IBD flare-ups
hidden_gut_defect_ibd.summary: Researchers identified a smoldering molecular defect in gut cells that persists during remission, potentially driving future inflammatory bowel disease flare-ups.
highlights: The defect involves abnormal cell‑death signaling detectable in patients who appear to be in remission
Study analyzed ~900 gut biopsies from 80 individuals and used patient‑derived organoids to validate findings
Stronger cell‑death signals correlated with higher relapse risk over a two‑year follow‑up
Findings could enable earlier prediction of flare‑ups and more personalized IBD management

hr8799_fifth_companion.headline: Gaia Uncovers Fifth Substellar Companion Around Young Star HR 8799
hr8799_fifth_companion.summary: Combining Gaia astrometry with Hipparcos data and radial velocities reveals a 10–14 Jupiter‑mass object at ~2–3 au, filling the detection gap in HR 8799.
highlights: Mass estimated at 10‑14 Jupiter masses
Orbit lies between 0.3 and 6 au, most likely 2‑3 au
Fits within low‑eccentricity resonant chain of the four known outer planets
Explains inner edge of the warm debris belt

arxiv_2609_21810v1.headline: JWST Detects CO2 and H2O in Hot Saturn WASP‑52b Amid Spotty Starlight
arxiv_2609_21810v1.summary: Using JWST NIRSpec G395H, astronomers have identified CO2 and H2O signatures in the atmosphere of the hot Saturn WASP‑52b despite contamination from its active K‑dwarf host.
highlights: First >10σ detection of CO2 with log abundance ≈ ‑5.09
H2O confirmed at ~3‑4σ with log abundance ≈ ‑3.41
Unocculted starspots required to explain a steep near‑infrared slope
Inhomogeneous high‑altitude clouds cover ~40 ± 20% of the terminator

arxiv_2609_21854v1.headline: Supernovae Confirmed as Primary Drivers of Galactic Turbulence in Andromeda
arxiv_2609_21854v1.summary: A new FAST and VLA HI survey of M31 identifies 118 superbubbles, showing supernova energy injection matches turbulence dissipation across the galaxy.
highlights: 118 superbubbles detected across M31’s disk with ages up to 40 Myr
Kinetic energy injection rates of 10^{49}–10^{51.5} erg kpc^{-3} Myr^{-1} derived from the bubbles
These rates closely match independently measured turbulence dissipation rates
Clustered supernova feedback alone can sustain galaxy‑scale turbulence

arxiv_2609_21881v1.headline: JWST Time‑Resolved Spectroscopy Reveals Thermal and Chemical Variability in Coldest Brown Dwarf
arxiv_2609_21881v1.summary: Using 11‑hour JWST NIRSpec/G395M observations, researchers retrieved temperature changes up to 100 K and shifting CO, PH₃, CO₂ abundances in WISE 0855‑07.
highlights: Thermal structure varies by ~1–<100 K between 0.4 and 10 bar pressures
CO abundance shows epoch‑to‑epoch fluctuations
Possible PH₃ and CO₂ changes modulate specific molecular features
Variability detected across the 3–5.2 µm mid‑infrared range

arctic_melt_season_length_levels_off.headline: Arctic Melt Season Length Stabilizes After Decades of Extension
arctic_melt_season_length_levels_off.summary: A NASA-led analysis shows the Arctic melt season, now about 40 days longer than in 1979, has plateaued since 2010 despite ongoing climate warming.
highlights: Melt season lengthened by ~40 days since 1979, with most growth before 2010
Stabilization driven by later freeze‑up rather than earlier melt‑onset
Changing cloud patterns since 2010 reduced solar heating, increasing variability

2609_21118v1.headline: Ion Energy in Relativistic Electron‑Positron‑Ion Reconnection Found Below Equipartition
2609_21118v1.summary: A new analytic theory and PIC simulations show ion energy scales with μ^{1/3}σ^{2/3}, often far below ion‑lepton equipartition in relativistic reconnection.
highlights: Ion mean energy follows μ^{1/3}(σ)^{2/3} when escaping non‑relativistically
Ion energy approaches lepton energy in the ultrarelativistic escape regime
Energy partition matches simulations across composition, mass ratio, and magnetization
Reduced ion share limits hadronic and neutrino emission from reconnection‑powered sources

proton_oxygen_collisions_cosmic_ray_mode.headline: CERN’s ATLAS Measures Proton‑Oxygen Collisions to Sharpen Cosmic‑Ray Air‑Shower Models
proton_oxygen_collisions_cosmic_ray_mode.summary: Physicists at CERN used the LHC’s ATLAS detector to record proton‑oxygen collisions, revealing that existing shower simulations miss key particle‑production details.
highlights: ATLAS recorded particle yields and angles from proton‑oxygen collisions at unprecedented precision
Measured cross section sits at the low end of seven model predictions, matching only two
No current model fully reproduces the observed particle multiplicities, with some off by a factor of ten

2609_20941v1.headline: Binary Evolution Models Reveal Multiple Small Kicks in White Dwarf Formation
2609_20941v1.summary: Analysis of Gaia DR2 and DR3 wide binaries shows that white dwarfs receive at least ten random 0.7 km/s kicks during the TP‑AGB phase.
highlights: Synthetic binary populations reproduce observed separation distributions of WD‑MS and WD‑WD pairs
Eccentricity data favor a random‑walk velocity model for WD‑MS binaries
No model matches the eccentricity distribution of WD‑WD binaries
At least ten episodic, randomly directed kicks yield a cumulative RMS velocity of ~0.7 km/s

gravity_decoherence_test.headline: Deep‑Underground Test Finds No Gravity‑Induced Decoherence Signal
gravity_decoherence_test.summary: A 62‑day run of a high‑purity germanium detector at Italy’s Gran Sasso laboratory saw no faint radiation predicted by the Károlyházy gravity‑decoherence model.
highlights: The experiment was conducted deep underground at INFN‑LNGS, shielding it from cosmic‑ray background.
Researchers looked for the tiny electromagnetic radiation that spacetime fluctuations would generate if Károlyházy’s model were
After 62 days of data, no such signal was observed, ruling out this version of gravity‑induced decoherence.

2609_20921v1.headline: ALMA ACE Survey Maps Gas Metallicity Relation at Cosmic Noon
2609_20921v1.summary: Using CO(3‑2) observations of 26 star‑forming galaxies at z ≈ 2, researchers find stellar mass chiefly drives chemical evolution while gas and star formation play secondary roles.
highlights: 26 main‑sequence galaxies (median log(M_) = 9.96) observed with ALMA
17 CO detections include some of the lowest‑metallicity CO sources at cosmic noon
Stellar mass explains most metallicity variance (σ≈0.10)
Molecular gas and SFR each contribute similarly (σ≈0.11‑0.13)
Average outflow mass‑loading factor η ≈ 4 inferred

ace_dust_content_cosmic_noon.headline: ALMA ACE Survey Finds Unexpectedly High Dust Masses in Subsolar‑Metallicity Galaxies at Cosmic Noon
ace_dust_content_cosmic_noon.summary: A new ALMA study of 25 star‑forming galaxies at z≈2.3 reveals dust masses around 10⁸ M⊙, three‑to‑nine times larger than comparable local galaxies.
highlights: Dust masses average 10⁸ M⊙, far exceeding local counterparts at similar metallicity
Dust‑to‑stellar mass ratio stays near 10⁻²·² regardless of metallicity
Specific star‑formation rates above 10⁻⁸ yr⁻¹ drive the elevated dust‑to‑stellar ratios

2609_21333v1.headline: Patchy Reionization Delays Star‑Formation Quenching in Isolated Ultra‑Faint Dwarfs
2609_21333v1.summary: High‑resolution zoom‑in simulations show that a radiative‑transfer patchy reionization model postpones quenching in ultra‑faint dwarf galaxies by roughly 440 Myr compared with uniform UV background.
highlights: Patchy reionization model delays quenching by ~440 Myr on average.
Uniform UVB simulations truncate star formation abruptly at reionization onset.
Extended star formation leaves no clear signature in stellar metallicity distribution.
Results align with recent observational constraints on Local Group ultra‑faint dwarf star‑formation histories.

nuclear_spin_swap_entanglement.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
nuclear_spin_swap_entanglement.headline: Nuclear‑spin swap boosts room‑temperature entanglement lifetime by 240‑fold
nuclear_spin_swap_entanglement.summary: Researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China swapped electron entanglement into silicon‑29 nuclei, extending coherence to over 240 µs at room temperature.
highlights: Entanglement persisted for more than 240 µs after transfer to nuclear spins, versus ~1 µs in the electron alone
The SWAP‑gate protocol retained 92.5% fidelity, only slightly below the initial 94%
Over 10% of 200 surveyed silicon‑carbide color centers hosted two or more strongly coupled silicon‑29 nuclei

exoplanet_radio_detection.headline: Radio Bursts Detected Directly from Exoplanet Beta Pictoris b Reveal Powerful Aurorae
exoplanet_radio_detection.summary: Using MeerKAT, astronomers captured rapid radio bursts from the gas giant Beta Pictoris b, confirming auroral emission and measuring a magnetic field around 1,250 gauss.
highlights: First unambiguous radio detection localized to an exoplanet rather than its host star
Signals match auroral processes expected for a planet orbiting close to its star
Estimated magnetic-field strength of Beta Pictoris b is ~1,250 gauss, far exceeding Jupiter’s 4.3 gauss
Observation made with South Africa’s MeerKAT array, a precursor to the Square Kilometre Array

alzheimer_mri.headline: MRI Reveals Subtle Cortical Thickening Up to Seven Years Before Alzheimer’s Diagnosis
alzheimer_mri.summary: Researchers found that individuals who later develop high amyloid‑beta levels show a few hundredths of a millimeter thicker cortex up to seven years prior to PET‑confirmed disease.
highlights: Cortical thickness differences of only a few hundredths of a millimeter were detectable up to seven years before amyloid‑beta
Study analyzed MRI data from over a thousand participants in long‑term aging cohorts
Both groups showed natural age‑related thinning, but future Alzheimer’s cases thinned less overall
Findings suggest early-stage inflammation may cause transient cortical thickening

equivalence_principle_tests.headline: Space‑borne atom interferometer delivers most precise quantum test of Einstein’s equivalence principle
equivalence_principle_tests.summary: A cold‑atom interferometer on the China Space Station achieved a 2.8 × 10⁻⁸ uncertainty, confirming the weak equivalence principle for 85Rb and 87Rb isotopes.
highlights: Cold atom interferometry on the China Space Station measured a differential acceleration of –2.7 × 10⁻⁷ between 85Rb and 87Rb
The experiment collected over 9,700 interference‑fringe pairs during a 280‑day mission
A separate Quantum Galileo Interferometer in Israel verified the same gauge phase for a free‑falling 87Rb wavepacket
Both studies were published in Science Advances and report peer‑reviewed results
The teams plan next‑generation tests using nanodiamond particles to probe higher‑mass quantum objects

brain_two_organs_discovery.headline: Stanford Study Shows Human Brain Developed from Two Separate Evolutionary Organs
brain_two_organs_discovery.summary: Researchers discovered that distinct progenitor cells form the forebrain and hindbrain, revealing an ancient split that reshapes our understanding of brain development.
highlights: Forebrain and midbrain arise from Otx2‑expressing progenitors, while hindbrain derives from Gbx2‑expressing cells
Team grew functional human hindbrain motor neurons in vitro for the first time
Evolutionary analysis shows the two‑origin pattern exists in chickens, zebrafish and acorn worms

early_mars_water_systems.headline: Perseverance Finds Complex Multi‑Stage Water Interactions in Mars’ Jezero Crater Margin Unit
early_mars_water_systems.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover uncovered igneous rocks in Jezero’s Margin Unit that record at least three distinct water events, reshaping ideas of early Martian habitability.
highlights: SuperCam laser analyses of 185 bedrock targets revealed sequential water‑rock reactions
Olivine-rich rocks show carbonate and silica formation from groundwater and lake water
Fluorite‑bearing veins indicate a later hot, underground water episode
Findings published in Communications Earth & Environment challenge prior carbonate‑only models

direct_imaging_subparsec_binary_smbhs_ng.headline: VLBA Images Reveal Sub-Parsec Binary Supermassive Black Holes in NGC 5044
direct_imaging_subparsec_binary_smbhs_ng.summary: VLBA observations have directly imaged two compact, flat‑spectrum radio cores separated by 0.38 pc, constituting the tightest binary AGN ever seen.
highlights: Two radio cores show flat spectra and variability
Separation measured at 0.38 parsec, an order of magnitude tighter than previous binaries
Observations span 4.9, 8.4, 15.2 and 23.6 GHz frequencies

2609_22466v1.headline: Model‑Independent Probe Reveals Baryon Depletion Around Galaxies via Lensing and kSZ
2609_22466v1.summary: A new technique combining DESI galaxy‑galaxy lensing with ACT kinematic Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich maps measures radial gas fractions, finding significant baryon loss relative to the cosmic mean.
highlights: Detected baryon depletion with signal‑to‑noise ratios of 17.1 (BGS) and 15.8 (LRG)
Method applies identical ΔΣ aperture filters to shear and kSZ temperature maps
Results lie between the strongest (Illustris‑1) and weaker feedback models from six simulations
Robust against splits by stellar mass and central versus satellite galaxies

gc_gamma_ray_and_neutrino_multi_messenge.headline: HAWC and IceCube Probe Galactic Center Gamma Rays for Neutrino Signals
gc_gamma_ray_and_neutrino_multi_messenge.summary: Using 2860 days of HAWC data and 12 years of IceCube muon-track observations, researchers find no neutrino excess from the Galactic Center, setting first upper limits.
highlights: HAWC detects gamma‑ray emission up to >100 TeV from the Galactic Center region
Analysis reveals a point source HAWC J1745‑2857 plus diffuse Galactic emission
IceCube’s 12‑year muon‑track data show no corresponding neutrino signal, placing an upper limit ~12× the predicted flux
The limit does not yet rule out the optically thin hadronic scenario for PeV cosmic‑ray acceleration

extreme_precision_radial_velocity_survey.headline: Galactic‑scale extreme‑precision radial velocity survey targets subgiant stars to map Milky Way acceleration
extreme_precision_radial_velocity_survey.summary: A new ESPRESSO survey of quiet subgiant stars within one kiloparsec aims to measure Galactic accelerations with ~50 cm s⁻¹ precision over a decade.
highlights: ESPRESSO on the VLT achieved ~70 cm s⁻¹ precision, now improved to ~50 cm s⁻¹
The "gold" sample comprises subgiant stars selected for minimal stellar jitter
Survey seeks direct constraints on the Milky Way’s dark‑matter distribution

grb_220706a_month_long_engine.headline: GRB 220706A Shows Record‑Breaking Month‑Long Engine and Bright Supernova
grb_220706a_month_long_engine.summary: Observations of GRB 220706A reveal central engine activity lasting 27 days in its rest frame and a super‑luminous supernova peaking at M_r ≤ ‑20.25.
highlights: X‑ray flares persisted until ≈51 days after trigger, the longest engine activity recorded
Redshift z = 0.8577 places the event at a cosmological distance
The associated supernova rivals SN 2011kl in brightness, fitting the super‑luminous class

thermal_relic_constraints_from_desi_lyma.headline: DESI Lyman‑α Forest Tightens Limits on Sterile Neutrinos and Extra Radiation
thermal_relic_constraints_from_desi_lyma.summary: Using DESI DR1 Lyman‑α power spectrum with Planck 2018 CMB and DESI DR2 BAO data, researchers find no evidence for extra relativistic species or sterile neutrinos.
highlights: Combined DESI DR1 1D Lyα power spectrum with Planck 2018 CMB and DESI DR2 BAO measurements.
Upper bound N_eff < 3.41 (95% credibility) shows no extra radiation.
Sterile neutrino effective mass constrained to m_s^eff < 0.061 eV.
ΔN_eff limits imply decoupling temperatures as high as the QCD epoch.

2609_23428v1.headline: Dark Matter Subhalos Could Skew Gravitational‑Wave Lens Time Delays
2609_23428v1.summary: Millisecond‑precise gravitational‑wave observations reveal that subhalos of 10⁶–10⁹ M☉ can perturb lensing time delays by several hours, challenging current analyses.
highlights: NFW‑profile subhalos introduce hour‑scale time‑delay anomalies in fold and cusp lens configurations
Current GW detectors achieve millisecond timing, far finer than the few‑hour precision of electromagnetic lensing
Statistical analysis of 200 realizations shows no milli‑images, but predicts measurable delay perturbations

2609_22424v1.headline: Quasar Outflows Linked from Broad‑Line Region to Galactic Scales
2609_22424v1.summary: A study of 148 ultra‑luminous quasars (Lbol > 10^47 erg s⁻¹, z ≈ 2–6.5) finds correlated CIV emission and BAL velocities, indicating BLR clouds accelerate to galaxy‑scale outflows.
highlights: Statistically significant correlations between CIV emission v98 and BAL vmin,BAL/vmax,BAL were detected.
High‑redshift quasars show larger CIV line shifts, broader profiles, and faster BAL outflows than lower‑redshift counterparts.
The sample spans redshifts z ≈ 2–6.5, probing cosmic‑time evolution of AGN‑driven winds.

inflated_sms_lrds.headline: JWST’s Little Red Dots May Be Inflated Supermassive Stars Pre‑cursor to Black Holes
inflated_sms_lrds.summary: New 1D models suggest metal‑rich supermassive stars with inflated envelopes could explain JWST’s abundant high‑redshift little red dots and seed supermassive black holes.
highlights: Models with metallicity Z≈10⁻² produce envelopes at Teff≈7000 K
Maximum non‑rotating masses reach 3×10⁵ Msun, luminosities ~10⁴⁴ erg s⁻¹
If each LRD collapses, predicted remnant density is ~10⁻² cMpc⁻³

stereoscopic_gravitational_wave_probe.headline: Gravitational‑Wave Lensing by AGN Disks Offers Dual‑View of Binary Mergers
stereoscopic_gravitational_wave_probe.summary: If many compact binary coalescences occur in active galactic nucleus accretion disks, their gravitational waves can be lensed to produce two distinct viewing angles detectable by current and future detectors.
highlights: LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA may observe multiple GW "images" from a single binary orbiting a supermassive black hole
The two images differ in effective viewing angle and exhibit a relativistic Doppler shift
A single extra parameter suffices to model AGN‑lens systems when the AGN spin aligns with the binary’s orbital angular momentum

wavedriver_lgs_ao.headline: WaveDriver Concept Shows Feasibility for Laser‑Guide‑Star AO on Habitable Worlds Observatory
wavedriver_lgs_ao.summary: Initial modeling and testbed experiments indicate the WaveDriver laser guide star system can achieve the picometer‑level wavefront stability required for the Habitable Worlds Observatory.
highlights: High Contrast Testbed demonstrated stability metrics approaching the required picometer precision
Multiple deformable mirrors and coronagraphs were integrated to assess sensor performance
Optical model quantifies LGS brightness, conjugation errors, and field errors from finite beacon separation

2609_23091v1.headline: Super‑Earth Interiors Contract by ~10% as Silicate Mantles Crystallise
2609_23091v1.summary: New PROTEUS simulations show that volatile‑poor super‑Earths shrink by about ten percent during mantle solidification, largely independent of mass.
highlights: Silicate interiors of 1‑10 Earth‑mass super‑Earths contract ~10 % as they cool
Volatile‑rich planets ≥5 Earth masses may retain deep magma oceans, limiting contraction
Contraction depends on mantle thinning, not host star irradiation or initial thermal state
